Page 2 — Pipeline Landscape, Identifiers, and Alert Taxonomy

Pipeline landscape and identifiers
Meridian Capital maintains a canonical naming convention to simplify monitoring and reporting. Each pipeline identifier encodes business domain, dataset, and frequency, ensuring consistent correlation across metrics, logs, and tickets. The convention is descriptive and minimizes ambiguity during cross-team reviews.

Parameter set — Identifier schema
- Format: ETL_{DOMAIN}_{DATASET}_{FREQUENCY}
- Domains (examples): FIN, RISK, TRSY, RET
- Datasets (examples): GL, PD, LCR, CARDS
- Frequencies: INTRADAY, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY
- Tag set (minimum): application=etl, pipeline_id, dataset, domain, env, owner, criticality

Primary workflow categories
- Ingestion: Source extracts from governed upstreams into staging zones using standardized connectors and manifests.
- Transformation: Batch transformations executed on managed compute or warehouse pushdown with lineage annotations.
- Load: Materialization into curated layers and downstream marts, with row-count and checksum signals emitted.
- Data quality: Rule evaluations for freshness, completeness, and referential consistency; results surfaced as metrics and dashboard tiles.
- Business validation: Finance and Risk steward attestations captured as status flags aligned to cutoff calendars.

Metrics dictionary (extract; see Appendix C for comprehensive list)
- job_start_lag_seconds: Time difference between scheduled start and actual start of a job within a pipeline.
- job_duration_seconds: Elapsed processing time for a job execution.
- pipeline_success_ratio: Ratio of successful jobs to total jobs in the last defined window.
- data_freshness_lag_seconds: Age of the most recent successful load compared to expected data timestamp.
- row_count_delta_ratio: Proportional change in loaded row counts relative to a rolling baseline.
- dq_rule_pass_ratio: Percentage of data quality rules passing in the last run.
- retry_count: Number of task retries observed for the current execution window.

SLO catalog excerpt (Prod, 2026-07 snapshot)
- ETL_FIN_GL_DAILY: Completion by 05:30 UTC on business days; freshness lag under 60 minutes; dq_rule_pass_ratio >= 0.98; monthly target: 99% adherence.
- ETL_RISK_PD_INTRADAY: Windowed delivery every hour between 06:00–20:00 UTC; end-to-end latency under 20 minutes; dq_rule_pass_ratio >= 0.99; monthly target: 99.5% adherence.
- ETL_TRSY_LIQ_WEEKLY: Completion by Monday 12:00 UTC; data completeness flagged for all inputs; dq_rule_pass_ratio >= 0.97; monthly target: 99% adherence.

Parameter set — Alert taxonomy (KB-ETL-2147-aligned)
- Severity P1: Material impact to regulatory submission timing or finance close; immediate OCC visibility; PD-SVC-ETL-PROD-01.
- Severity P2: High priority degradation risking SLO breach for critical datasets; OCC summary flag on DD-Board-ETL-Prod-042.
- Severity P3: Non-critical schedule drift or transient freshness variance; tracked in weekly OCC summary.
- Severity P4: Informational deviations and post-change annotations; consolidated in monthly review.

Signal Taxonomy

Signals are grouped to ensure consistent thresholding and incident routing. Each signal category includes standard labels: component_id, environment (prod/non-prod), dataset, owner_team, and severity_candidate.

- Availability: Binary liveness and health checks for schedulers, agents, and endpoints.
- Latency: End-to-end and segment durations relative to SLOs; includes schedule delay and run time.
- Volume: Record counts, file counts, and bytes processed; measured against rolling baselines.
- Quality: Completeness, uniqueness, validity against data contracts; summarized via percentile scores.
- Schema Drift: Additions, removals, or type changes in inbound structures; contract variance is flagged.
- Backlog: Queue depth and unprocessed work units relative to time-based drains.
- Freshness: Age of latest successful partition/publication versus consumer expectations.

3. Alert Routing and Severity Model

Alerting adheres to a standardized severity model calibrated to customer impact, data timeliness, and regulatory considerations. Severity levels determine notification channels, response time objectives, and status reporting cadence. All production alerts must reference a Monitor ID and include required labels (component_id, dataset, environment, owner_team, severity_candidate, region).

Severity Matrix

- SEV-1 (Critical): Material impact on regulatory or revenue-sensitive datasets; missed freshness SLO p99; complete pipeline halt without workaround.
  Response Objective: Engage Incident Command within 5 minutes; executive notification required.
  Routing: SRE Primary + ETLOPS + Data Leadership bridge.
  Ticket: Auto-create Major Incident (MI) — prefix MC-DATA-MI-.

- SEV-2 (High): Degradation impacting SLO p95; partial pipeline failure; repeat retries exceeding budget; consumer publish latency beyond threshold for priority marts.
  Response Objective: Acknowledge within 10 minutes; recovery actions prioritized.
  Routing: ETLOPS On-Call + owning data domain.
  Ticket: Incident (INC) — prefix MC-DATA-INC-.

- SEV-3 (Moderate): Isolated task failures with successful retries; small variance from volume baselines; non-critical data set delays.
  Response Objective: Acknowledge within 30 minutes; monitor and mitigate.
  Routing: Owning team; informational to SRE.
  Ticket: Service Request or Problem (SR/PRB) upon recurrence.

- SEV-4 (Low/Info): Transient anomalies, known maintenance windows, expected seasonal effects.
  Response Objective: No immediate action; catalog for trend analysis.
  Routing: Owner only.
  Ticket: Optional knowledge entry (KB-DATA-).

Alert Lifecycle States

Alerts progress through standardized operational states for accountability and auditability. All state transitions are captured in the Monitoring Registry and mirrored in the incident ticket.

Lifecycle State Definitions

- Firing: Signal exceeds defined threshold; alert created with contextual labels and recent metric snapshots.
- Acknowledged: An engineer has accepted responsibility; timer shifts from “time to page” to “time to mitigate.”
- Mitigated: Underlying signal returned to within threshold; post-mitigation observation begins.
- Resolved: Incident ticket closed following validation checklist; residual risk logged if applicable.
- Verified: Post-resolution validation by owner or DQO confirms data consumer readiness.

Overview
Data freshness and latency monitors verify that pipeline outputs arrive within agreed service windows and reflect recent source activity. This section defines canonical metrics, environment parameters, monitoring thresholds, and the routine review cadence adopted by Data Platform Operations (DPO) and Enterprise Data Engineering (EDE). Page 6: Volume and Schema Drift Monitoring

Overview
Volume and schema drift monitors ensure that data completeness and structural consistency remain within expected bounds for each dataset and ingest feed. Volume monitors detect anomalous record counts, partition sparsity, or distributional changes. Schema drift monitors detect column additions/removals, data type changes, and primary key constraint violations. This section covers baseline calculations, anomaly parameters, review cadence, and the decision matrix for triage.

Signal Definitions
- Volume Delta (%): Relative difference between observed record_count and expected baseline for the same business date and comparable weekday/season.
- Null Ratio (%): Proportion of nulls in critical fields compared to baseline tolerance.
- Duplicate Rate (%): Fraction of records breaching declared uniqueness constraints.
- Schema Change: Detected modification to column set or types versus the catalog contract at runtime.
- Key Violation: Existence of duplicate business keys in the output partition.

Anomaly Engine Parameters
| Parameter                      | Default (Tier-1)      | Default (Tier-2)      | Notes                                                |
|--------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Baseline Window                | 28 days rolling        | 21 days rolling        | Seasonality-aware (weekday weighting)                |
| Sensitivity (Z-score)          | 2.5                    | 3.0                    | Lower value = higher sensitivity                     |
| Minimum Counts (records)       | 10,000                 | 2,000                  | Avoids spurious alerts on small partitions           |
| Null Ratio Tolerance           | +2.0 p.p.              | +3.5 p.p.              | Absolute percentage point delta vs baseline          |
| Duplicate Rate Tolerance       | +0.25 p.p.             | +0.50 p.p.             | Applies to business keys                             |
| Suppression Window (cooldown)  | 45 minutes             | 30 minutes             | Prevents alert storms for the same root cause        |
| Change Ticket Linkage Required | Yes                    | Yes                    | Schema changes require prior CHG reference           |

Executive overview
This report documents the current-state lineage and provenance across priority financial domains for Meridian Capital during Q2 2026. Coverage emphasizes end-to-end traceability of critical data assets supporting statutory and management reporting, with particular focus on Treasury Liquidity, Market Risk, and Regulatory Capital subject areas. The scope includes dataset- and field-level lineage where available, dependency maps for ingestion and transformation layers, and operational evidence of data quality monitoring. The content is designed to support internal attestations (quarterly control confirmations) and to inform continuous improvement tasks already planned for Q3 2026.

Highlights for the period:
- 96.4% lineage completeness across the in-scope subject areas (up from 93.1% in Q1), measured by the proportion of columns with documented upstream origin at least two hops back to source-of-record.
- 100% job-level provenance capture for orchestrated transformations in Finance Analytics workspaces (Airflow and Databricks jobs tagged and linked to business glossary terms).
- Reduction in “unknown source” flags from 41 to 9 through remediation of historical ingestion identifiers and standardization of dataset keys in Bronze and Silver layers.
- No material data control breaches reported; two non-material variances noted and resolved within SLA (details provided on page 2).

- Provenance controls: run-to-run job identifiers, source snapshot tags, and record counts reconciled against ingestion manifests; non-production environments excluded from metrics.

Page 10 — Section 3.5 Reference Data Provenance & Downstream Impact: FX Spot Rates (DSET-FXR-0007)

Scope
This section documents the lineage and provenance for FX_Spot_Rates_EOD (DSET-FXR-0007) and its composite derivative Rate_Composite_V2 (DSET-FXR-0012), as used across settlement, P&L, and risk calculations during Q2 2026. The review was coordinated by Enterprise Data Governance (EDG) with Market Data Engineering (MDE) and Risk Analytics (RA), tracked under MC-DL-2421. The objective was to confirm column-level traceability from vendor delivery through internal normalization, verify business rule transparency, and assess downstream impact of two minor schema adjustments introduced in May.

Provenance Statement
- Primary vendor: Refinitiv (Contract VND-RFT-2024-112)
- Delivery modality: Scheduled secure data feed, daily 22:15 UTC; file-based format with checksum manifest
- Secondary vendor (fallback): Bloomberg (Contract VND-BBG-2024-077), used conditionally for missing pairs
- Ingestion pipeline: PIPE-FXR-PRD-003@v3.2.1; normalizes vendor payload, enforces ISO currency codes, deduplicates by symbol-date
- Composite pipeline: PIPE-FXR-PRD-004@v2.8.0; selects primary rate; applies fallback if primary missing; stamps provenance attributes

Schema and Column Mapping (selected)
- asof_date (DSET-FXR-0007.asof_date) ← vendor.delivery_date (normalized to UTC date)
- ccy_pair (DSET-FXR-0007.ccy_pair) ← concat(base_ccy, quote_ccy)
- mid_rate (DSET-FXR-0007.mid_rate) ← (bid + ask)/2 when both present; else vendor mid
- source_vendor (DSET-FXR-0007.source_vendor) ← literal “Refinitiv” at load time
- composite_mid (DSET-FXR-0012.composite_mid) ← if primary mid_rate present then mid_rate else fallback_mid
- provenance_tag (DSET-FXR-0012.provenance_tag) ← “RFT” if primary, “BBG” if fallback; includes load_id reference

Operational Metrics (Q2 to Date)

- Completeness (pairs per business day): median 176; interquartile range: 4; target ≥ 170 — met
- Fallback activation rate: 0.7% of pair-days; threshold ≤ 2.0% — within bounds
- Data freshness to consumers (P95): 00:24:18 post-delivery; SLO ≤ 00:30:00 — met

Exception Review
- Incident INC-2026-08841 (2026-05-17): Missing AUD/JPY and CAD/SEK from primary vendor for 30 minutes post-cutoff. Composite pipeline applied fallback automatically; provenance_tag = “BBG” for 2 pairs. Downstream variance in P&L explained by Market Risk (RA-Ticket RA-PL-3021). Root cause: vendor-side delay; no internal processing fault. Status: Resolved; Post-incident review PIR-2026-052 completed 2026-05-24.
- Advisory ADV-2026-019 (2026-05-28): Precision increase per CHG-2026-04271 required minor cast adjustments in consumer semantic views. EDG bulk scan confirmed 7 affected views; BI Engineering updated by 2026-06-01 under tasks BI-SV-1104..1110.

Downstream Consumers (selected) and Declared Dependency Paths

Production Deployment Runbook v3.1
Meridian Capital

Document ID: MRC-RB-PROD-00031
Version: 3.1
Effective Date: 2026-07-15
Prepared by: Release Engineering (RELENG)
Primary Stakeholders: Digital Banking (DB), Capital Markets Technology (CMT), Enterprise Platform Services (EPS), Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Information Risk Office (IRO)

Executive Summary
This runbook governs the production deployment of Release 2026.07-B for Meridian Capital’s Digital Banking portfolio. The objective is to promote approved application components to the Production environment within the authorized window, with minimal service interruption and measurable adherence to operational quality gates. The document captures applicable approvals, scope boundaries, coordination plans, pre-deployment readiness confirmations, and the metrics framework for post-deployment validation.

The deployment is designed as a standard, low-complexity change per Change Risk Model v2.4, with an expected total active change duration under 90 minutes. No customer-impacting downtime is anticipated. All customer-facing updates have been conducted through feature toggles validated in lower environments.

Release and Change Parameters

- Release Name: 2026.07-B
- Change Ticket: MRC-CHG-04873 (CAB Approved)
- CAB Session: CAB-3125 (2026-07-10 14:00 UTC)
- Deployment Window: 2026-07-23 00:30–02:00 UTC (Approved by OPS-SCHED-2207)
- Scope Identifier: DB-PRD-SCOPE-0921
- Environments In-Scope: PROD (clusters PRD-EU-1, PRD-US-2), DR not in scope
- Artifact Registry Tag: REL-2026.07-B.15
- Rollback Package: RLB-2026.06-E (pre-validated)
- Release Train: Q3 Cycle A
- Change Type: Standard, Pre-Authorized Template ST-DB-001

Change Content Summary
The release includes non-breaking service updates and housekeeping changes across Digital Banking services. Functionality changes remain behind inactive flags in production. Schema evolution steps are forward-compatible and confirmed reversible through migration plan MIG-DB-146, with dry runs passing in PreProd. No infrastructure topology changes are included. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds are updated to align with new log attributes.

Component Scope Table

- Component: Payments API (svc-payments)
  Version: 3.18.0
  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-PA
  Notes: Performance enhancement; no API contract changes
- Component: Customer Profile (svc-customer)
  Version: 2.11.4
  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-CP
  Notes: Logging key standardization; feature flags dormant
- Component: Notification Orchestrator (svc-notify)
  Version: 1.9.2
  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-NO
  Notes: Retry policy tuning; alert mapping update
- Database Migration: MIG-DB-146
  Applied To: Customer Profile read replica set
  Notes: Adds nullable column; forward-compatible

Purpose and Scope
This runbook provides operational structure for deployment execution by SRE and RELENG under the guidance of the Release Manager. It records pre-conditions, authorizations, responsibility assignments, and verification checkpoints. It excludes design details, source code changes, and sensitive configurations. Disaster recovery validation is out of scope for this window and is tracked under DR-TEST-2039.

- Platform saturation (memory avg): 62% (headroom policy target: <= 75%)

Change Window Controls
The deployment adheres to freeze policy FP-OPS-07, which allows standard changes within an approved window outside of peak retail hours. Auto-scaling policies remain in steady-state; no capacity adjustments requested. Error budgets are currently healthy for all in-scope services. Incident management bridge is pre-provisioned.

Operational Notes
- No data backfills required for this release.
- No third-party vendor involvement in the window.
- Support runbook references: RB-OBS-002 (dashboards), RB-SRE-009 (bridge etiquette), RB-REL-004 (artifact signoff traceability).

Executive Summary
This runbook governs the production deployment of Release 2026.07-B for Meridian Capital’s Digital Banking portfolio. The objective is to promote approved application components to the Production environment within the authorized window, with minimal service interruption and measurable adherence to operational quality gates. The document captures applicable approvals, scope boundaries, coordination plans, pre-deployment readiness confirmations, and the metrics framework for post-deployment validation.

The deployment is designed as a standard, low-complexity change per Change Risk Model v2.4, with an expected total active change duration under 90 minutes. No customer-impacting downtime is anticipated. All customer-facing updates have been conducted through feature toggles validated in lower environments.

Release and Change Parameters

- Release Name: 2026.07-B
- Change Ticket: MRC-CHG-04873 (CAB Approved)
- CAB Session: CAB-3125 (2026-07-10 14:00 UTC)

Change Content Summary
The release includes non-breaking service updates and housekeeping changes across Digital Banking services. Functionality changes remain behind inactive flags in production. Schema evolution steps are forward-compatible and confirmed reversible through migration plan MIG-DB-146, with dry runs passing in PreProd. No infrastructure topology changes are included. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds are updated to align with new log attributes.

This runbook provides operational structure for deployment execution by SRE and RELENG under the guidance of the Release Manager. Production Deployment Runbook v3.1
Meridian Capital

Document ID: MRC-RB-PROD-00031
Version: 3.1
Effective Date: 2026-07-15
Prepared by: Release Engineering (RELENG)
Primary Stakeholders: Digital Banking (DB), Capital Markets Technology (CMT), Enterprise Platform Services (EPS), Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Information Risk Office (IRO)

Executive Summary
This runbook governs the production deployment of Release 2026.07-B for Meridian Capital’s Digital Banking portfolio. The objective is to promote approved application components to the Production environment within the authorized window, with minimal service interruption and measurable adherence to operational quality gates. The document captures applicable approvals, scope boundaries, coordination plans, pre-deployment readiness confirmations, and the metrics framework for post-deployment validation.

The deployment is designed as a standard, low-complexity change per Change Risk Model v2.4, with an expected total active change duration under 90 minutes. No customer-impacting downtime is anticipated. All customer-facing updates have been conducted through feature toggles validated in lower environments.

Release and Change Parameters

- Release Name: 2026.07-B
- Change Ticket: MRC-CHG-04873 (CAB Approved)
- CAB Session: CAB-3125 (2026-07-10 14:00 UTC)
- Deployment Window: 2026-07-23 00:30–02:00 UTC (Approved by OPS-SCHED-2207)
- Scope Identifier: DB-PRD-SCOPE-0921
- Environments In-Scope: PROD (clusters PRD-EU-1, PRD-US-2), DR not in scope
- Artifact Registry Tag: REL-2026.07-B.15
- Rollback Package: RLB-2026.06-E (pre-validated)
- Release Train: Q3 Cycle A
- Change Type: Standard, Pre-Authorized Template ST-DB-001

Change Content Summary
The release includes non-breaking service updates and housekeeping changes across Digital Banking services. Functionality changes remain behind inactive flags in production. Schema evolution steps are forward-compatible and confirmed reversible through migration plan MIG-DB-146, with dry runs passing in PreProd. No infrastructure topology changes are included. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds are updated to align with new log attributes.

Component Scope Table

- Component: Payments API (svc-payments)

  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-PA
  Notes: Performance enhancement; no API contract changes
- Component: Customer Profile (svc-customer)
  Version: 2.11.4
  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-CP
  Notes: Logging key standardization; feature flags dormant
- Component: Notification Orchestrator (svc-notify)
  Version: 1.9.2
  Change Ref: REL-2026.07-B-NO
  Notes: Retry policy tuning; alert mapping update
- Database Migration: MIG-DB-146
  Applied To: Customer Profile read replica set
  Notes: Adds nullable column; forward-compatible

Purpose and Scope
This runbook provides operational structure for deployment execution by SRE and RELENG under the guidance of the Release Manager. It records pre-conditions, authorizations, responsibility assignments, and verification checkpoints. It excludes design details, source code changes, and sensitive configurations. Disaster recovery validation is out of scope for this window and is tracked under DR-TEST-2039.

Change Window Controls
The deployment adheres to freeze policy FP-OPS-07, which allows standard changes within an approved window outside of peak retail hours. Auto-scaling policies remain in steady-state; no capacity adjustments requested. Error budgets are currently healthy for all in-scope services. Incident management bridge is pre-provisioned.

The risk profile is low, based on historical stability of the services and successful lower-environment rehearsals. The following entries are tracked in RSK-REG-2026-Q3.

Environment and Dependency Overview
Deployments target production clusters PRD-EU-1 and PRD-US-2 via the standard pipeline. The window is set for 90 minutes, aligning with the standard change cadence. No overlapping maintenance activities are scheduled according to OPS-CAL-PRD-0723. Internal Audit — Quantitative Systems FY2026
Meridian Capital
Document ID: MC-IA-QS-2026-01 | Distribution: Internal (Confidential) | Prepared by: Internal Audit (Technology & Operations)

1. Executive Summary
This report presents the results of Internal Audit’s review of Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (“QS”) for Fiscal Year 2026, conducted by the Internal Audit Technology & Operations practice in coordination with Audit Analytics and Model Risk Audit. Fieldwork was performed between 2026-04-08 and 2026-06-21, with closing discussions finalized on 2026-07-03 14:30 UTC (Ref: IA-WP-2026-4471; Meeting Minutes MM-IA-2026-0703). The audit assessed the design and operating effectiveness of selected IT general controls, service management processes, data quality monitoring practices, and model lifecycle interfaces embedded in the QS platform. Based on procedures performed, the overall conclusion is Satisfactory, with opportunities for improvement noted in documentation consistency, evidence traceability, and non-critical operational metrics alignment. No High or Critical risk-rated issues were identified. Two Moderate and three Low observations were raised, each supported by management-accepted action plans and tracked under Jira Epic QSR-IA-2026-E01.

The QS platform under review supports front-office and risk functions by providing pricing analytics, scenario generation, factor modeling, batch computations, and data services to downstream consumers. The environment is operated by Quantitative Engineering (QE) with partner functions in Platform Reliability Engineering (PRE), Enterprise Data Office (EDO), and Model Risk Management (MRM). The audit examined controls across change management, incident/problem management, access recertification, data lineage documentation, operational resilience measures, model code migration interfaces, and vendor assurance of key third-party services that underpin computational workloads and market data sourcing. The review period covered 2025-10-01 through 2026-05-31, with selected look-back and look-forward procedures as warranted.

The audit rated control design as Effective, with generally Effective operating effectiveness. Control evidence was consistently available in the firm’s standard repositories (Confluence space QS-CONF, SharePoint library IA-EVID-QS-2026) and referenced by ticketing systems (ServiceNow, Jira). Sample testing confirmed adherence to defined approval thresholds, segregation of duties, and release gates in scope areas. Observations primarily relate to completeness of operational documentation, minor inconsistencies in metric definitions across dashboards, and standardization opportunities in record retention tagging. Management has initiated remediation activities (Jira: QSR-7096, QSR-7120, QSR-7144), with target dates between 2026-09-30 and 2026-11-15. No policy exceptions were requested or granted during the audit period (Ref: TRC-PE-Register, extract 2026-06-18 09:11 UTC).

2. Scope and Objectives
The audit scope encompassed systems and processes categorized under the Quantitative Systems domain as defined in the Enterprise Application Inventory (EAI) on 2026-03-29 (EAI Export ID: EAI-2026-QS-029). In scope systems included: QS-Core (APP-QS-001) providing pricing and analytics services; QS-Stream (APP-QS-002) managing ingestion, transformation, and publishing of market and reference data; QS-Calc (APP-QS-003) orchestrating batch/grid computations for end-of-day and intraday risk; QS-UI (APP-QS-004) user-facing tools for scenario configuration; Model Catalog Connector (APP-QS-006) facilitating model registration metadata to MRM repositories; and associated data pipelines and job schedulers declared under the QS domain. Interfaces to Risk Data Warehouse (RDW), Trade Processing Services (TPS), and Regulatory Reporting Extracts (RRE) were reviewed at a control-interface level to validate adequacy of handoffs and accountability boundaries.

Objectives were to: assess the design and operating effectiveness of change and release management across QS; evaluate incident and problem management processes and SLAs; verify access governance, including joiner-mover-leaver and quarterly recertification; review data quality monitoring and lineage documentation for critical data elements (CDEs) within QS-Stream; verify resiliency practices for business-critical components (as defined by Business Impact Analysis, BIA-QS-2026-RevC); and review the interface controls between QE deployments and MRM’s independent model validation lifecycle for relevant code and configuration artifacts. The audit also performed a targeted review of third-party assurance coverage for critical service providers supporting computational workloads and data provisioning.

3. Methodology and Standards
The audit was conducted in accordance with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Standards and the Meridian Capital Internal Audit Methodology (IA-METH-2024-02). Control criteria were mapped to Meridian Technology Risk & Controls (TRC) policies, including SDLC and Change (TRC-SDLC-001), Access Governance (TRC-AG-002), Service Management (TRC-SM-003), Data Governance (EDO-DG-001), and Resilience (TRC-BCP-005). Procedures included document reviews, control walkthroughs, data analytics on ticketing systems, and sample-based testing. A combined sample of 25 normal changes (CHG00348726, CHG00349110, CHG00349603, et al.), 6 emergency changes (CHG-E004412 to CHG-E004417), 20 incidents (INC00295108, INC00295744, et al.), and 6 problems (PRB0004419 to PRB0004424) were examined for conformance to approval workflows, peer review evidencing, release packaging traceability, and post-implementation verification. For access governance, 12 joiner/mover/leaver requests (AR-102949 to AR-102960) and the Q2 recertification attestation (AG-RC-2026-QS, attested 2026-05-07 16:02 UTC) were reviewed for alignment to least-privilege roles and timely attestation. For data quality, 14 active monitors (DQ-QS-Stream-001 to -014) and lineage documentation for five CDEs (CDE-QS-001 PriceSourceID; CDE-QS-004 ValuationDate; CDE-QS-009 RiskBucket; CDE-QS-012 TradeIDRef; CDE-QS-017 CurveFamily) were sampled to validate defined rules, thresholds, stewardship assignments, and incident routing.

Data analytics were performed against exports from ServiceNow (Report ID: SN-EXP-IA-QS-2026-14, extracted 2026-06-10 12:05 UTC) and Jira (Filter: project = QSR and created >= 2025-10-01, export timestamp 2026-06-12 09:52 UTC). No system credentials were requested or used by audit; all access to evidence occurred through read-only enterprise repositories with standard entitlements. Interviews were held with QE, PRE, EDO, and MRM representatives between 2026-04-16 and 2026-06-07 (Interview Log IA-INT-QS-2026, entries IL-034 to IL-061). Consistency checks were executed to reconcile deployment tags with change requests, and to verify closure notes align to testing artifacts and release communications.

4. Governance and Organizational Context
Quantitative Systems are owned by Quantitative Engineering (QE), reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, Markets & Research Technology. Oversight is provided through the Quantitative Systems Steering Committee (QSSC), meeting monthly with representation from QE, PRE, EDO, MRM, Technology Risk & Controls (TRC), and Lines of Business stakeholders from Markets Risk. The QSSC charter (QSSC-CH-2026-01, revised 2026-01-15) defines decision rights for prioritization, release scheduling windows, and acceptance of non-functional requirements. Operating procedures reference enterprise policies for SDLC, change, access, and incident management. Performance reporting is consolidated by PRE into a monthly scorecard (QS-OPS-SCORE-YYYYMM) tracking deployment cadence, mean time to resolution (MTTR), job success rates, and SLA adherence for data delivery.

The audit noted that governance artifacts were current, accessible, and appropriately approved. Meeting minutes and decisions (QSSC-MM-2026-02 through QSSC-MM-2026-06) were filed within two business days of each session and included clear action owner assignments. Interfaces with Model Risk Management are formalized via the Model Deployment Interface Procedure (MRM-QE-IF-2025-07), which separates responsibilities for code lineage, parameter configuration, and independent validation checkpoints. While documentation quality was generally strong, an opportunity exists to further standardize references to data quality monitors within QSSC decision logs to reinforce traceability from business priorities to technical control adjustments (captured as Observation L3 in Section 8).

5. Timeline and Logistics
Planning was initiated on 2026-03-18 (IA Plan ID: IA-PLAN-2026-QS-01). The opening conference was held 2026-04-08 15:00–15:45 UTC (Invitation Ref: IA-MTG-2026-0408-QS), and interim status updates were provided on 2026-05-03 and 2026-05-31. Fieldwork concluded on 2026-06-21 with a preliminary readout to management on 2026-06-25 13:00 UTC. The closing meeting occurred on 2026-07-03 14:30 UTC. Evidence collection windows were communicated and tracked via ServiceNow task group TSK-GRP-IA-QS-2026 (tasks TSK008411 to TSK008468). All evidence items were version-controlled and time-stamped upon receipt. No delays impacted the audit timeline beyond a two-business-day reschedule of the QE capacity planning walkthrough (rebooked from 2026-05-09 to 2026-05-11 due to participant conflicts).

6. System Overview
The Quantitative Systems platform comprises services and pipelines that deliver analytics and curated data to front-office, risk, and finance consumers. Core components include QS-Core (APP-QS-001), an API-driven analytics layer for pricing, sensitivities, and scenario outputs; QS-Stream (APP-QS-002), an ingestion and transformation framework for market and reference data; QS-Calc (APP-QS-003), a batch/grid computation orchestrator supporting end-of-day and intraday cycles; QS-UI (APP-QS-004), presentation tools for scenario configuration and monitoring; and the Model Catalog Connector (APP-QS-006), which synchronizes registration metadata and lifecycle states with MRM repositories. Environments are segregated by lifecycle (Development, Integration, UAT, Production) with standard promotion controls and artifact tagging. Business criticality ratings per BIA-QS-2026-RevC classify QS-Core and QS-Calc as Tier 1 services, QS-Stream as Tier 2, and QS-UI/Connector as Tier 3. Data classification within QS-Stream includes Firm Confidential and Public categories as defined in the Enterprise Data Classification Standard (EDO-CLASS-2024). No sensitive personal data resides in the platform per the Privacy Impact Assessment PIA-QS-2025-01, reaffirmed 2026-02-27.

Integration points with the Risk Data Warehouse (RDW) and Regulatory Reporting Extracts (RRE) follow standardized publish/subscribe patterns with documented schemas and release communications. Operational responsibilities are split between QE (development, release, configuration of models and analytics) and PRE (runtime operations, monitoring, incident coordination). EDO provides stewardship for CDEs flowing through QS-Stream, ensuring data quality rules are cataloged and aligned to enterprise standards. Model Risk Management maintains independence and oversight for model validation and governs the Model Catalog, with defined checkpoints for code artifact identification and deployment readiness.

7. Control Environment Summary
Change and release management processes for QS follow TRC-SDLC-001 and TRC-SM-003. Standard changes require peer review, automated testing evidence, impact assessments, and approval from designated change approvers; emergency changes require post-implementation review within two business days. Observed adherence in sampled changes included traceable links from change requests to deployment tags and regression testing artifacts. Release communications were disseminated through the established channel (DL-QS-Release-Notice) at least 24 hours prior to production implementation, with closures documented in ServiceNow. Access governance aligns to TRC-AG-002 with role-based access mapped to defined entitlements; quarterly recertification was completed for Q2 FY2026 (AG-RC-2026-QS, attested by QE and PRE managers). Service management incorporates incident and problem workflows with SLA tracking, service health dashboards, and retrospective reviews for Sev2 events.

Data governance is anchored by EDO-DG-001 and includes stewardship assignments, lineage documentation, and data quality monitoring. For QS-Stream, rule definitions and thresholds are documented in the Data Quality Catalog (DQ-CAT-QS-Stream, version 2026.05). Operational resilience for Tier 1 services includes documented recovery objectives, runbooks, and scenario testing per TRC-BCP-005. Third-party assurance for critical services is tracked under Vendor Risk Management (VRM) with the latest SOC reports reviewed and mapped to control coverage matrices (VRM-ASSUR-2026-QS).

8. Sampling and Metrics Overview
Samples were selected using stratified criteria to capture peak periods, varied severities, and different deployment windows. The 25 standard changes (e.g., CHG00348726 closed 2026-03-12 21:14 UTC; CHG00349603 closed 2026-04-19 02:46 UTC) evidenced required approvals and test artifacts. Of the 6 emergency changes (CHG-E004413 raised 2026-04-28 04:22 UTC; CHG-E004416 raised 2026-05-17 19:08 UTC), all completed post-implementation reviews within the expected timeframe, with one instance requiring a clarifying addendum added within one business day (CHG-E004416 Addendum Note AN-2026-0519). Incident sampling (20 items; INC00295108 opened 2026-02-09 07:30 UTC; INC00295744 opened 2026-03-01 11:15 UTC) reflected MTTR within target for Sev3 and Sev4, and within extended target for one Sev2 incident due to dependency on a third-party data feed (variance documented in INC00295744 Post-Incident Review PIR-2026-0303). Problem investigations (PRB0004419 to PRB0004424) demonstrated root cause analysis and prevention actions registered in Jira (QSR-7002, QSR-7011).

Access requests sampled (AR-102949 to AR-102960) aligned to least-privilege roles with evidence of manager approval and fulfillment by PRE. The Q2 recertification evidenced timely attestations and removal of two dormant entitlements within five business days of attestation closure (Deprovision tickets TSK008462, TSK008463). Data quality monitors reviewed (DQ-QS-Stream-001 Price Completeness; DQ-QS-Stream-006 Reference ID Conformity; DQ-QS-Stream-014 Timeliness) met defined thresholds in 96.8% of observed daily cycles across the period, with flagged thresholds routed through incident workflows. Vendor assurance artifacts for two critical providers were current (SOC 2 Type II period ending 2025-12-31; review notes VRM-REV-2026-021 and -029 dated 2026-04-22 and 2026-05-16).

Key operational metrics, as presented in the QS-OPS scorecards for 2026-02 through 2026-05, indicate: average monthly deployments to Production of 11.5; emergency change rate at 2.1% of total changes; incident volume averaging 14 per month with Sev2 comprising 7%; Sev2 MTTR median of 2.9 hours; batch job success rate for QS-Calc at 99.2% over the review period; and SLA adherence for data delivery windows at 98.6% for QS-Stream Tier 1 feeds. Variances between the PRE dashboard and QE’s internal tracker for two months were reconciled as reporting boundary differences (included/excluded retry counts). A standardization action has been logged under QSR-7120 to align metric definitions across teams by 2026-09-30.

9. Summary of Preliminary Observations
Two Moderate observations and three Low observations were raised:

- Observation M1: Evidence retention tagging for change-related artifacts is inconsistently applied across Jira Epics QSR-Release-24.03 and QSR-Release-24.04, leading to extended retrieval times. Design remains sound; operating practice requires standardization of references to canonical evidence locations. Management action: Implement evidence-link templates and periodic spot checks (QSR-7096; target 2026-10-15).

- Observation M2: Minor discrepancies in runbook version references between QS-Calc and QS-Stream during two handoffs (Runbook IDs RB-QS-Calc-2026.04 vs RB-QS-Stream-2026.03) were identified in incident closures INC00295744 and INC00296017. While operational impact was contained, alignment of version metadata in closures and dashboards will improve traceability. Management action: Enforce version metadata validation in closure checklist (QSR-7144; target 2026-11-15).

- Observation L1: SLA measurement boundaries differ between PRE dashboard (includes job retries) and QE time-series tracker (excludes retries) for QS-Stream, causing minor variance in reported monthly adherence. Management action: Standardize calculation methodology and glossary (QSR-7120; target 2026-09-30).

- Observation L2: Model deprecation calendar entries were not consistently referenced in two release notes (RN-QS-2026-04B, RN-QS-2026-05A), although MRM records were accurate. Management action: Update release note template to include a model lifecycle section (QSR-7113; target 2026-08-31).

- Observation L3: QSSC decision logs do not consistently cross-reference CDE-level data quality monitors when approving prioritization changes for QS-Stream. Management action: Add CDE/DQ reference fields to QSSC minutes (QSR-7131; target 2026-09-15).

10. Limitations
The audit relied on samples and representations current as of the fieldwork period. Penetration testing and code-level secure development reviews were out of scope and covered by separate assurance functions; results from those functions were not re-performed. The audit did not independently re-execute production changes or replay historical data loads. Conclusions should be interpreted in the context of sampled evidence, observed during the specified timeframe, and may not reflect changes implemented after 2026-06-21.

Follow-up on management action plans will be conducted per Internal Audit procedures, with verification checkpoints scheduled for October and November 2026 (IA-FUP-PLAN-QS-2026, created 2026-07-05 10:22 UTC). No immediate risk escalation is warranted based on current findings.

Internal Audit — Quantitative Systems FY2026
Meridian Capital

Page 3

1. Audit Scope and Objectives
The Internal Audit function conducted a risk-based review of Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (QS) operating environment for Fiscal Year 2026, emphasizing governance, model lifecycle control execution, computational workflow reliability, data handling practices, and incident/change management integration. The scope encompassed end-to-end control activities supporting analytics used by Risk, Treasury, and Finance, including model inventory maintenance, model development and deployment governance, validation closure tracking, data ingestion and transformation quality checks, scheduling and monitoring of batch and intraday processes, and issue/remediation management. User access provisioning and segregation of duties for QS platforms were validated at a high level to confirm coordination with Enterprise Identity & Access Management; a detailed access management evaluation remains subject to a separate audit in FY2026 H2.

Objectives were to (i) assess the design and operating effectiveness of key controls supporting model accuracy, reproducibility, and timeliness; (ii) confirm alignment to internal policies and applicable industry frameworks; (iii) evaluate the completeness and currentness of the QS model inventory and its linkage to validation and performance monitoring records; and (iv) determine whether operational metrics and escalations are consistently captured and reported to governance forums. The period under review was 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30, with certain prior-period artifacts examined to establish control continuity where relevant.

2. Audit Universe and Entities In-Scope
The audit universe included the following QS capabilities and affiliated functions:
- Quantitative Engineering (QE): model build pipelines, packaging, and runtime orchestration; ticket refs QS-2120 through QS-2195.
- Model Risk Management (MRM): policy oversight, independent validation, and performance monitoring attestations; evidence set MRM-EVD-2026-QS-03.
- Risk Analytics Operations (RAO): scheduling, job monitoring, and runbook execution for daily/weekly cycles; ServiceNow assignment group RAO-QSYS.
- Enterprise Data Office (EDO): upstream market/reference data intake stewardship and data quality (DQ) rule maintenance; DQ dashboard reference DQ-RPT-2026-05-31.
- Infrastructure & Reliability (I&R): platform availability SLAs and non-functional observability; change calendar artifact CHG-CAL-Q2FY26.

Systems and services logically associated with QS included the Market Data Normalization service (MDN), Curve Construction Engine (CCE), Scenario Generation Service (SGS), Risk Factor Aggregation (RFA), and the Batch Execution Scheduler (BES). Development and UAT environments were reviewed for promotion controls; Production was reviewed for operational controls, including incident management, change control, and dashboard reporting to senior stakeholders. Third-party vendor feeds were considered only insofar as they intersected with internal DQ controls.

3. Methodology and Standards Applied

6. Operating Environment Overview
The Quantitative Systems landscape supports daily, weekly, and ad hoc analytical runs for Market Risk, Counterparty Credit Risk, and Treasury liquidity monitoring. The environment comprises Development, UAT, and Production tiers with a standardized release calendar (primary window Wednesdays 20:00–22:00 UTC; secondary window Saturdays 10:00–12:00 UTC), coordinated through the Enterprise Change Advisory Board. The Batch Execution Scheduler (BES) orchestrates approximately 1,380 jobs on a typical business day, integrating dependencies across the Market Data Normalization (MDN), Curve Construction Engine (CCE), and Scenario Generation Service (SGS). Job-level telemetry feeds an operations dashboard reviewed by RAO at 07:30 UTC and 16:30 UTC, with on-time start and completion serving as key service indicators.

Data inputs are sourced from approved vendor feeds and internal reference repositories overseen by EDO. Data quality controls are applied at intake (schema conformance, timestamp windows) and transformation (key field completeness, continuity checks), with alerts routed to RAO and EDO assignment groups in ServiceNow. QS model artifacts are versioned and cataloged, with traceability from model inventory item to validation pack, deployment ticket, and production run identifier. Production monitoring emphasizes timeliness (SLA: 98.5% of critical jobs complete by 08:15 UTC), stability (critical incident MTTR target ≤ 120 minutes), and reproducibility (ability to re-run with consistent results given identical inputs and configurations).

The internal audit encompassed the Quantitative Systems operating landscape as provisioned for FY2026 planning and execution cycles. Business processes evaluated included model deployment gating (from Model Development to Production handoffs), change management (standard and emergency changes executed via Enterprise Change Management Office [ECMO]), incident and problem management (Production Assurance [PA] processes), data lineage documentation and approvals (Data Office governance workflows), and operational monitoring (availability, throughput, and data quality KPIs). Audit procedures relied on stratified sampling across change, incident, and deployment populations recorded during the period 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31. 2.4 Key Metrics and Control Objectives Reviewed
The audit assessed adherence to defined control objectives across availability, change governance, and data quality:

- Availability and Performance: Target ≥ 99.5% monthly service availability for QSTRAT and RG-NA; job success ratio ≥ 98.0%; 95th percentile job completion time within ±10% of baseline (baseline established FY2025Q4).
- Change Governance: 100% of standard changes with approved risk/impact assessment and back-out plan attached pre-implementation; emergency changes ratified within two business days; segregation of duties enforced between code authors and approvers in MGE.
- Data Quality and Lineage: ≥ 99.0% feed completeness for in-scope market and reference data sets; timeliness within contractual SLAs; lineage documentation current and approved for all critical data elements (CDEs) consumed by QSTRAT.

All seven emergency changes were post-facto ratified within the two-business-day requirement (average 0.8 days). Data quality measures indicated 99.2% average feed completeness across five key data sets (MD-Core, RF-Static, FX-Spot, SecMaster-L3, and Calendar-Holiday), with three isolated timeliness deviations discussed in Section 4.

Internal control testing for Quantitative Systems covered key IT general controls (ITGCs) and process-level controls relevant to financial reporting. The test window spanned 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-15, with populations drawn from production changes, access certifications, and operational reconciliations. Controls were selected based on the FY2026 scoping memo (IA-Scope-QS-2026 v1.3) and mapped to control IDs in the Controls Library (CLIB-QS).

- QS-SOX-ITGC-07: User Access Review — Quarterly certification of privileged access to QS production environments by System Owners and Risk Data Owners. Population: 61 privileged accounts. Sample: 25. Result: Effective. Evidence included signed certifications (CERT-2026Q2-QS-PRD) and access attestations in SailPoint (AAR-2026-05-QS). One sampling item required clarification of functional need for a temporary elevation; documentation was updated under ticket ACC-20260603-221 with closure on 2026-06-06T14:19:22Z.

- QS-IC-12: Code Promotion Segregation — Promotion approvals segregated from development activities and evidenced via ServiceNow workflow. Population: 97 relevant changes. Sample: 30. Result: Effective. All sampled changes showed distinct initiator and approver groups, with MRM sign-off for model-affecting items. No deviations noted.

- QS-IC-21: Data Reconciliation — Monthly reconciliation of risk aggregates to Finance ledgers at desk level with variance thresholds and documented resolution. Population: 2 months. Sample: 2 (April, May 2026). Result: Effective. Variance analyses were complete, signed by RAO and Finance Controllers, and resolved within policy timeframes.

- QS-IC-33: Job Scheduler Integrity — Preventive controls to restrict unauthorized modifications to critical job chains. Population: 12 critical chains. Sample: 6. Result: Effective. Change logs and approval evidence present; no direct edits outside of approved windows.

- QS-SOX-ITGC-09: Change Management — Formal change records with impact assessment, testing evidence, and rollback plans. Population: 164 QS environment changes (inclusive of infrastructure patches and configuration updates). Sample: 35. Result: Effective with Observation. While all samples contained requisite artifacts, three promotion records referenced legacy test summary formats; ProdCtl has standardized the template as of 2026-05-27 (TEM-CHG-2026.05). Documentation uplift is tracked under DOC-20260601-311 with completion confirmed by 2026-06-09T09:58:04Z.

Testing procedures adhered to Internal Audit Methodology v2026.02, with cross-referencing to system-of-record evidence repositories. No deficiencies were identified. Two housekeeping observations regarding consistency of evidence indexing and the use of updated templates were communicated to management; management accepted and has actioned them. Based on the testing performed, control design and operating effectiveness for scoped controls are rated Effective.

3.7 Vendor and Third-Party Services Oversight

Vendor dependencies for QS include market data providers, analytics libraries, and managed compute services. The Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) framework requires annual due diligence, contract alignment to service levels, and monitoring of operational performance. For FY2026 to date, all Tier 1 and Tier 2 QS vendors completed due diligence packages (TPRM cases TPR-2026-1413 through TPR-2026-1422). The audit reviewed a targeted set encompassing a market data feed provider, an analytics component vendor, and a managed platform service.

Service level adherence for market data feeds was evaluated against contracted delivery windows and data quality commitments. Monthly vendor scorecards (VSC-2026-04 to VSC-2026-06) indicated on-time delivery at 99.6%, with two partial delays in May acknowledged by the provider and communicated via incident reports. Operational impacts were mitigated through established QS timeliness safeguards and calendar offsets. No contractual remedies were invoked; DQC minutes recorded the events and closeout.

For the analytics component vendor, license reconciliation and version alignment were validated. Entitlement usage reports (LIC-QS-2026Q2) showed consumption within licensed quantities, and upgrade roadmaps were tracked against QS change plans under CHG-20260612-1843. Dependency scanning and operational validation were documented prior to lower-environment deployments, with Production promotion scheduled during a standard window and gated by MRM impact confirmation. No exceptions or unplanned deviations were observed.

The managed platform service underwent a performance and capacity review as part of the Q2 vendor oversight cadence. KPIs on compute allocation, storage throughput, and incident response times remained within thresholds. Evidence of business continuity testing by the vendor (BCP attestations V-BCP-2026-Q2) was present and current. TPRM recorded timely refresh of cybersecurity posture questionnaires and certifications in May 2026, and InfoSec Advisory indicated no action items specific to QS dependencies. Contractual SLAs pertaining to operational availability and support responsiveness were aligned with QS service definitions, and there were no changes to service scope.

Vendor governance artifacts were complete: meeting minutes (VEN-OPS-2026-05, VEN-OPS-2026-06), action trackers, and performance dashboards were maintained and shared with QS stakeholders. The audit notes favorable collaboration among QEng, RAO, and TPRM in maintaining vendor oversight hygiene. The overall vendor oversight posture for QS is assessed as Satisfactory.

3.8 Business Continuity and Capacity Management

Business continuity arrangements for Quantitative Systems consist of active-active compute clusters across primary and secondary availability zones, data replication aligned to defined recovery objectives, and documented procedures for workload redirection. The Q2 FY2026 continuity exercise (BCX-QS-2026-02) executed at 2026-05-11T01:00:00Z validated controlled redirection of the overnight risk window to the secondary zone. Target recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes and recovery point objective (RPO) of ≤5 minutes were met; observed figures were 43 minutes and ≤2 minutes respectively. Post-exercise reports, including execution logs and business validation sign-offs from Risk Management and Finance, were complete (BCX-REP-20260512). The exercise also verified catalog completeness for continuity documentation and updated contact rosters.

Capacity management practices are formalized under QS-CAP-01, with quarterly planning cycles led by ProdCtl and Platform Engineering. Utilization trend analyses for Q2 exhibited stable headroom on compute and storage resources across critical windows. Forecasting scenarios were presented to the QS Governance Committee on 2026-06-06, reflecting anticipated data volume growth tied to new risk factor coverage planned for Q3. To accommodate growth, a pre-approved capacity uplift for the risk compute cluster will be executed in August (PRQ-20260608-442), with pre-production validation scheduled in July during non-peak cycles. Monitoring dashboards (CAP-DASH-QS v2026.06) showed no hotspot indicators, and alert thresholds remained appropriately calibrated.

Backup and restore validations demonstrated consistent results. Weekly sample restores for key data domains (market data snapshots, model state stores, and audit logs) were performed per schedule, with integrity checks passing and completion certificates archived (BKP-VAL-2026-05-W2 through BKP-VAL-2026-06-W3). No missed cycles were identified. The audit observed the adoption of harmonized retention tagging across QS datasets, simplifying evidence retrieval and aligning with enterprise records management standards.

Operational resilience was further evidenced by dry-run execution of reduced-capacity mode for intraday analytics on 2026-06-01 (RES-DRY-2026-06-01). Performance remained within user-acceptable thresholds, and the cutback plan was signed off by RAO and QEng. Communications during the drill followed the established protocol, and no customer-facing impacts occurred. Documentation updates resulting from the drill were recorded under DOC-20260602-327 and closed within five business days.

Based on testing and evidence reviewed, QS business continuity and capacity management controls are operating effectively. Management demonstrates proactive planning for volume growth and disciplined execution of continuity exercises, with clear ownership, current documentation, and measurable outcomes.

4.2 Data Lineage and Quality Controls — Market and Reference Data

Scope and approach. The audit reviewed the completeness, accuracy, and timeliness controls governing market and reference data consumed by Quantitative Systems (QSYS) applications across pricing, risk, and analytics processes. In-scope datasets included Level-1 equity and FX spot feeds (IDs: MD-EQ-L1, MD-FX-L1), interest rate curves (MD-IR-CRV), and core security master attributes (REF-SECMASTER). We assessed upstream-to-downstream lineage as documented in the Enterprise Data Catalog (Atlas asset refs: ATLAS-ASSET-9F2C0B1E, ATLAS-ASSET-2C7D943A), and evaluated control design and operating effectiveness for the period 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-31. Evidence sources comprised: lineage diagrams and field mappings maintained by Data Engineering — Market Pipelines (DE-MP) in Confluence (pages DE-MP/MD-SCHEMA/2026Q1), ServiceNow change records (sample: CHG0011423, CHG0011511), JIRA work items (QSYS-2184, QSYS-2219, DE-MP-1447), and monitoring dashboards provided by Enterprise Logging & Observability (ELO) (dashboards: ELO-QS-MD-Overview v3.12).

Control design summary. Controls evaluated included automated schema drift detection at ingestion (alert rule: ELO-MD-SCHEMA-01), deduplication and late-arriving event handling in the curated layer (job: DAG_MD_EQ_L1_CURATE, run logs sampled 2026-02-11 22:07 UTC), staleness and freshness SLAs with pager escalation to QS Ops for Level-1 feeds (SLA: ≤15 minutes data freshness, measured at the point of consumption by QRM calculators), and periodic reconciliation of record counts between raw landing and curated tables (monthly QC cadence led by DE-MP). In addition, we reviewed procedures for symbol normalization and currency code mapping to internal symbology (referenced mapping set ID: MAP-SYM-2026.02) and assessed data retention configurations against the Enterprise Records Schedule (hot: 13 months; cold archive: 7 years).

Observations and results. Lineage documentation was complete and current for all in-scope pipelines. Asset-level lineage in Atlas correctly reflected vendor sources, intermediate transformations, and consuming applications (QRM-VaR, QRM-Stress, and QS-Analytics), including partitioning and enrichment steps. We observed consistent use of authoritative keys (instr_id, source_id) and timestamp attributes to ensure traceability. The visual lineage matched the operational flow as observed in Airflow runs for sampled dates, with no orphaned or ambiguous nodes. Minor variances in attribute naming conventions between the Atlas glossary and physical schema (e.g., “px_close” vs. “close_price”) were tracked under QSYS-2219 and scheduled for harmonization under CHG0011511 (deployed 2026-03-22 03:06 UTC with eCAB approval eCAB-2026-21).

Schema drift and data quality alerts were functioning as intended. During the period, four low-severity schema drift alerts were raised (ELO alert refs: ALERT-ELK-2026-1198, -1201, -1223, -1254) due to a vendor adding an optional commentary field to the FX feed and extending attribute length for an equity venue code. These changes were backward-compatible; no consumer impact was noted. Closeout activities included updating the schema registry documentation and performing regression checks (JIRA DE-MP-1447; release CHG0011488 on 2026-03-15 01:41 UTC). Audit review confirmed evidence of peer review and sign-off by QS Ops (approver: T. Nguyen, timestamp 2026-03-14 18:19 EST).

The deduplication and late-arrival logic operated within tolerance. A 90-day reconciliation sample (n=12 checkpoints) indicated average record variance of 0.03% between landing and curated layers, attributable to late-day vendor retransmissions near the UTC date boundary. The largest single-day variance (0.07% on 2026-02-06) was analyzed under incident MC-QS-INC-2026-0413 (opened 2026-02-06 21:03 UTC; resolved 2026-02-07 02:28 UTC). Root cause was a retransmit window overlap for Asia-Pacific equity markets coinciding with a maintenance restart at a downstream consumer. Mitigation included tightening the acceptance window by 2 minutes for the affected venue and adding post-curation reconciliation logs. No data loss or mispricing was observed; QRM consumers processed the corrected batch within the same operations cycle.

Staleness SLA adherence remained strong. For Level-1 FX and equity feeds, freshness compliance was 98.7% within the defined ≤15-minute SLA at point of consumption. Non-compliant intervals clustered around 2026-03-08 07:00–08:00 UTC during the Daylight Saving Time transition and a vendor-side heartbeat delay (vendor advisory REF-2026-031; QS Ops ticket QSYS-2184). The QS Ops bridge documented appropriate notification and monitoring posture; no downstream breaches of trading or risk calculation windows occurred. The audit corroborated that alerts reached on-call personnel within one minute of breach and that incident timelines were logged in Servicenow (INC0019283, opened 2026-03-08 07:06 UTC; resolved 08:02 UTC).

Reference data controls for symbology and currency mapping were satisfactory with a noted improvement action. We observed an isolated inconsistency where London Stock Exchange secondary listings were normalized to an obsolete internal venue code in the REF-SECMASTER mapping layer. The issue was detected by the monthly symbol health check (report QS-REF-HEALTH-2026-02, run 2026-02-20 10:00 UTC) and remediated via MAP-SYM-2026.02 uplift (CHG0011423, implemented 2026-03-11 21:04 UTC). The potential impact was limited to a non-critical exposure report that reads venue-level attributes; no valuation or risk metrics were affected. Management has committed to extending the symbol normalization regression suite to include venue code backfills for cross-listed instruments (action item QSYS-ACT-2026-011, due 2026-05-15; status: In Progress, 60% complete as of 2026-04-01 12:30 EST).

Retention and recovery controls conformed to policy. Sampled data restore tests from cold archive for MD-IR-CRV (request RST-2026-0031; executed 2026-03-05 13:22 UTC) completed within the targeted recovery time objective. Audit confirmed evidence of chain-of-custody logging for restored artifacts and timely data destruction post-validation.

Conclusion. Overall, data lineage and quality controls for market and reference data are effective. Documentation is current, alerting is appropriately tuned, and remediation workflows are timely. Minor enhancement opportunities exist in glossary-to-schema naming harmonization and expansion of symbol normalization regression coverage. These items do not materially affect control effectiveness and are actively tracked with clear owners and due dates.

4.3 Model Performance Monitoring — Backtesting and Stability

Scope and monitoring framework. The audit assessed the design and operating effectiveness of model performance monitoring across key QSYS models: Value-at-Risk (QRM-VAR-SR02), Stress Testing (QRM-STRESS-CRD), and an alpha generation module for systematic strategies (QRM-VAOG-AlphaV3). We reviewed backtesting results, PnL attribution coverage, alert thresholds, and governance workflows with Model Risk & Validation (MRV) and Quantitative Systems Operations (QS Ops) for the period 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31. Evidence included monitoring dashboards (QS Monitor v4.6; board QRM-MON-Board-12), MRV validation reports (MRV-VAL-2026-0041, issued 2026-02-28), and incident/problem tickets (INC0019551, PRB000472).

Backtesting results were within tolerance. The rolling 252-trading-day VaR backtest showed nine exceptions as of 2026-03-31, below the yellow threshold and consistent with the model’s risk appetite. Two exceptions fell within the audit window (2026-01-12 and 2026-03-14), coincident with outsized moves in rates and FX, respectively. MRV independently reviewed both exceptions (MRV-EXC-2026-0007, -0010) and confirmed alignment with market conditions, with no indication of model misspecification or data issues. Stress testing scenario coverage was expanded during the period to include a commodities shock vector (CHG0011537; eCAB-2026-22) per prior year recommendations; monitoring thresholds were recalibrated accordingly, and no false positives were introduced.

PnL explain and attribution coverage exceeded targets. For Q1 FY2026, daily PnL attribution coverage averaged 97.8% (target ≥95%), with residuals primarily linked to fees and execution slippage outside model scope. Exceptions were tracked under QSYS-2209 and closed with documentation by QS Analytics on 2026-03-19 16:44 EST. The monitoring platform flagged an elevated residual on 2026-02-22 (ALRT-QRM-2026-0312); investigation (INC0019462) traced the variance to a delayed dividend adjustment ingestion. DE-MP confirmed correction in the subsequent batch; no recurrences observed.

Model drift and stability indicators were adequately instrumented. For QRM-VAOG-AlphaV3, feature distribution drift indices ranged 0.92–1.05 during the review period, within the established control limits. A transient drift alert on 2026-01-19 14:08 UTC (ALRT-QRM-2026-0201) was escalated to MRV (ticket MRV-VAL-2026-0041) and resolved as non-material, stemming from a rebalancing-induced shift in factor exposures. The VaR computational pipeline met latency SLOs (p99 ≤480 seconds) except for two days (2026-03-03, 2026-03-09) when upstream batch durations extended following permitted platform changes (CHG0011589). QS Ops documented compensating controls through an extended observation window; no downstream reporting deadlines were breached.

Governance and re-approval. The VaR model (QRM-VAR-SR02) completed timely periodic re-approval on 2026-02-28 with conditions to evaluate an expanded stress window for select asset classes by mid-year (MRV condition set MRV-CND-2026-12). The action plan (QSYS-ACT-2026-017) designates joint ownership between MRV and QSYS for implementation and measurement, with interim checkpoints scheduled (2026-04-30 and 2026-06-15). As of 2026-04-01 09:55 EST, the plan is on track (45% complete), with preliminary scenario backfill completed and calibration testing underway (JIRA QRM-TEST-329).

Conclusion. Monitoring controls for model performance, drift, and backtesting are effective. Alerts are calibrated to business risk, responses are timely, and documentation supports traceability. The SLO variances observed were attributable to approved upstream changes and were managed without customer or regulatory impact.

4.4 Change Management — Release Cadence and Control Effectiveness

Scope and population. We evaluated releases affecting the QSYS production estate (applications: QRM-VaR, QRM-Stress, QS-Analytics; platforms: QSYS-Core, Data Ingestion) executed from 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-31. The audit tested 30 changes from a population of 184 production changes (ServiceNow CHG population extract SNAP-CHG-QSYS-2026Q1, generated 2026-04-02 08:12 EST), covering standard, normal, and emergency categories.

Cadence and approvals. Normal changes followed the defined Tuesday/Thursday 20:00–23:00 ET windows with eCAB approvals recorded under eCAB-2026-07, -14, -21. Change records consistently contained business justification, risk assessments, and backout plans. Segregation of duties was effective: in all tested samples, developers and approvers were distinct, with approvals from authorized roles (Technology Risk Office, Production Assurance). Build artifacts were appropriately referenced (Jenkins job QS-CI-Release build #982, completed 2026-02-18 01:12 UTC), and pre-implementation testing evidence was present for 29/30 sampled changes (96.7%). The exception (CHG0011607) lacked an attached functional test summary at approval time; the artifact was subsequently uploaded (2026-02-19 10:22 EST) with eCAB notation and no adverse outcomes.

Execution quality and post-implementation review. Change failure rate for the quarter was 0.6% (1 of 184), with a single change rolled back due to a validation query error in a non-critical reporting job (CHG0011554; associated incident INC0019520 opened 2026-03-05 00:37 UTC; resolved 03:41 UTC). Emergency changes (n=3: CHG0011734, CHG0011798, CHG0011831) were appropriately invoked in response to vendor-side anomalies and executed under expedited approvals, followed by mandatory retrospectives documented by Production Assurance (PA-SO-2026-0252, -0261, -0267). All three retrospectives identified clear preventive actions, which were tracked to closure in JIRA (QSYS-2231, QSYS-2237, DE-MP-1479).

Control evidence and linkage to operational stability. Post-implementation monitoring evidence (30–60 minute observation logs with sign-offs) was present in 100% of sampled standard/normal changes. Where incidents occurred within 24 hours of change (n=4; INC0019459, INC0019481, INC0019520, INC0019568), mean time to resolve was 3.2 hours, and root cause attribution was completed within two business days in each case. None of the incidents led to missed reporting deadlines or incomplete risk runs, and two were traced to external dependencies (vendor feed delays) rather than release defects. The change calendar reflected appropriate blackout observance around month-end risk cycles.

Process maturity and data quality of the change register. The change register was complete and timely, with accurate linkages to impacted configuration items and downstream applications. Minor inconsistencies were noted in the naming convention of deployment packages across QSYS-Core and Data Ingestion (e.g., QS-PLAT-2026.3.14 vs. QS-PLATFORM-2026_03_14), which can hinder automated reporting. Management has initiated a standardization exercise (QSYS-OPS-STD-2026-05) with a target effective date of 2026-06-30. Additionally, the free-text “success/failure rationale” field was sparsely populated in 5 of 30 sampled records; while evidence existed elsewhere, completing this field would strengthen auditability.

Conclusion and rating. Change management controls are effective. Approvals are timely, segregation of duties is maintained, and execution quality is high with a low failure rate. Minor enhancements to artifact attachment discipline and naming standardization are underway and, in our assessment, do not materially impact control effectiveness. Management has accepted the observations with remediation dates aligned to Q3 FY2026 and designated accountable owners within QS Ops and DE-MP.

Internal Audit — Quantitative Systems FY2026
Meridian Capital
Document ID: MC-IA-QS-2026-01 | Distribution: Internal (Confidential) | Prepared by: Internal Audit (Technology & Operations)

1. Executive Summary
This report presents the results of Internal Audit’s review of Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (“QS”) for Fiscal Year 2026, conducted by the Internal Audit Technology & Operations practice in coordination with Audit Analytics and Model Risk Audit. Fieldwork was performed between 2026-04-08 and 2026-06-21, with closing discussions finalized on 2026-07-03 14:30 UTC (Ref: IA-WP-2026-4471; Meeting Minutes MM-IA-2026-0703). The audit assessed the design and operating effectiveness of selected IT general controls, service management processes, data quality monitoring practices, and model lifecycle interfaces embedded in the QS platform. Based on procedures performed, the overall conclusion is Satisfactory, with opportunities for improvement noted in documentation consistency, evidence traceability, and non-critical operational metrics alignment. No High or Critical risk-rated issues were identified. Two Moderate and three Low observations were raised, each supported by management-accepted action plans and tracked under Jira Epic QSR-IA-2026-E01.

The QS platform under review supports front-office and risk functions by providing pricing analytics, scenario generation, factor modeling, batch computations, and data services to downstream consumers. The environment is operated by Quantitative Engineering (QE) with partner functions in Platform Reliability Engineering (PRE), Enterprise Data Office (EDO), and Model Risk Management (MRM). The audit examined controls across change management, incident/problem management, access recertification, data lineage documentation, operational resilience measures, model code migration interfaces, and vendor assurance of key third-party services that underpin computational workloads and market data sourcing. The review period covered 2025-10-01 through 2026-05-31, with selected look-back and look-forward procedures as warranted.

The audit rated control design as Effective, with generally Effective operating effectiveness. Control evidence was consistently available in the firm’s standard repositories (Confluence space QS-CONF, SharePoint library IA-EVID-QS-2026) and referenced by ticketing systems (ServiceNow, Jira). Sample testing confirmed adherence to defined approval thresholds, segregation of duties, and release gates in scope areas. Observations primarily relate to completeness of operational documentation, minor inconsistencies in metric definitions across dashboards, and standardization opportunities in record retention tagging. Management has initiated remediation activities (Jira: QSR-7096, QSR-7120, QSR-7144), with target dates between 2026-09-30 and 2026-11-15. No policy exceptions were requested or granted during the audit period (Ref: TRC-PE-Register, extract 2026-06-18 09:11 UTC).

2. Scope and Objectives
The audit scope encompassed systems and processes categorized under the Quantitative Systems domain as defined in the Enterprise Application Inventory (EAI) on 2026-03-29 (EAI Export ID: EAI-2026-QS-029). In scope systems included: QS-Core (APP-QS-001) providing pricing and analytics services; QS-Stream (APP-QS-002) managing ingestion, transformation, and publishing of market and reference data; QS-Calc (APP-QS-003) orchestrating batch/grid computations for end-of-day and intraday risk; QS-UI (APP-QS-004) user-facing tools for scenario configuration; Model Catalog Connector (APP-QS-006) facilitating model registration metadata to MRM repositories; and associated data pipelines and job schedulers declared under the QS domain. Interfaces to Risk Data Warehouse (RDW), Trade Processing Services (TPS), and Regulatory Reporting Extracts (RRE) were reviewed at a control-interface level to validate adequacy of handoffs and accountability boundaries.

Objectives were to: assess the design and operating effectiveness of change and release management across QS; evaluate incident and problem management processes and SLAs; verify access governance, including joiner-mover-leaver and quarterly recertification; review data quality monitoring and lineage documentation for critical data elements (CDEs) within QS-Stream; verify resiliency practices for business-critical components (as defined by Business Impact Analysis, BIA-QS-2026-RevC); and review the interface controls between QE deployments and MRM’s independent model validation lifecycle for relevant code and configuration artifacts. The audit also performed a targeted review of third-party assurance coverage for critical service providers supporting computational workloads and data provisioning.

3. Methodology and Standards
The audit was conducted in accordance with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Standards and the Meridian Capital Internal Audit Methodology (IA-METH-2024-02). Control criteria were mapped to Meridian Technology Risk & Controls (TRC) policies, including SDLC and Change (TRC-SDLC-001), Access Governance (TRC-AG-002), Service Management (TRC-SM-003), Data Governance (EDO-DG-001), and Resilience (TRC-BCP-005). Procedures included document reviews, control walkthroughs, data analytics on ticketing systems, and sample-based testing. A combined sample of 25 normal changes (CHG00348726, CHG00349110, CHG00349603, et al.), 6 emergency changes (CHG-E004412 to CHG-E004417), 20 incidents (INC00295108, INC00295744, et al.), and 6 problems (PRB0004419 to PRB0004424) were examined for conformance to approval workflows, peer review evidencing, release packaging traceability, and post-implementation verification. For access governance, 12 joiner/mover/leaver requests (AR-102949 to AR-102960) and the Q2 recertification attestation (AG-RC-2026-QS, attested 2026-05-07 16:02 UTC) were reviewed for alignment to least-privilege roles and timely attestation. For data quality, 14 active monitors (DQ-QS-Stream-001 to -014) and lineage documentation for five CDEs (CDE-QS-001 PriceSourceID; CDE-QS-004 ValuationDate; CDE-QS-009 RiskBucket; CDE-QS-012 TradeIDRef; CDE-QS-017 CurveFamily) were sampled to validate defined rules, thresholds, stewardship assignments, and incident routing.

Data analytics were performed against exports from ServiceNow (Report ID: SN-EXP-IA-QS-2026-14, extracted 2026-06-10 12:05 UTC) and Jira (Filter: project = QSR and created >= 2025-10-01, export timestamp 2026-06-12 09:52 UTC). No system credentials were requested or used by audit; all access to evidence occurred through read-only enterprise repositories with standard entitlements. Interviews were held with QE, PRE, EDO, and MRM representatives between 2026-04-16 and 2026-06-07 (Interview Log IA-INT-QS-2026, entries IL-034 to IL-061). Consistency checks were executed to reconcile deployment tags with change requests, and to verify closure notes align to testing artifacts and release communications.

4. Governance and Organizational Context
Quantitative Systems are owned by Quantitative Engineering (QE), reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, Markets & Research Technology. Oversight is provided through the Quantitative Systems Steering Committee (QSSC), meeting monthly with representation from QE, PRE, EDO, MRM, Technology Risk & Controls (TRC), and Lines of Business stakeholders from Markets Risk. The QSSC charter (QSSC-CH-2026-01, revised 2026-01-15) defines decision rights for prioritization, release scheduling windows, and acceptance of non-functional requirements. Operating procedures reference enterprise policies for SDLC, change, access, and incident management. Performance reporting is consolidated by PRE into a monthly scorecard (QS-OPS-SCORE-YYYYMM) tracking deployment cadence, mean time to resolution (MTTR), job success rates, and SLA adherence for data delivery.
