Internal Audit — Quantitative Systems FY2026
Meridian Capital
Document ID: MC-IA-QS-2026-01 | Distribution: Internal (Confidential) | Prepared by: Internal Audit (Technology & Operations)

1. Executive Summary
This report presents the results of Internal Audit’s review of Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (“QS”) for Fiscal Year 2026, conducted by the Internal Audit Technology & Operations practice in coordination with Audit Analytics and Model Risk Audit. Fieldwork was performed between 2026-04-08 and 2026-06-21, with closing discussions finalized on 2026-07-03 14:30 UTC (Ref: IA-WP-2026-4471; Meeting Minutes MM-IA-2026-0703). The audit assessed the design and operating effectiveness of selected IT general controls, service management processes, data quality monitoring practices, and model lifecycle interfaces embedded in the QS platform. Based on procedures performed, the overall conclusion is Satisfactory, with opportunities for improvement noted in documentation consistency, evidence traceability, and non-critical operational metrics alignment. No High or Critical risk-rated issues were identified. Two Moderate and three Low observations were raised, each supported by management-accepted action plans and tracked under Jira Epic QSR-IA-2026-E01.

The QS platform under review supports front-office and risk functions by providing pricing analytics, scenario generation, factor modeling, batch computations, and data services to downstream consumers. The environment is operated by Quantitative Engineering (QE) with partner functions in Platform Reliability Engineering (PRE), Enterprise Data Office (EDO), and Model Risk Management (MRM). The audit examined controls across change management, incident/problem management, access recertification, data lineage documentation, operational resilience measures, model code migration interfaces, and vendor assurance of key third-party services that underpin computational workloads and market data sourcing. The review period covered 2025-10-01 through 2026-05-31, with selected look-back and look-forward procedures as warranted.

The audit rated control design as Effective, with generally Effective operating effectiveness. Control evidence was consistently available in the firm’s standard repositories (Confluence space QS-CONF, SharePoint library IA-EVID-QS-2026) and referenced by ticketing systems (ServiceNow, Jira). Sample testing confirmed adherence to defined approval thresholds, segregation of duties, and release gates in scope areas. Observations primarily relate to completeness of operational documentation, minor inconsistencies in metric definitions across dashboards, and standardization opportunities in record retention tagging. Management has initiated remediation activities (Jira: QSR-7096, QSR-7120, QSR-7144), with target dates between 2026-09-30 and 2026-11-15. No policy exceptions were requested or granted during the audit period (Ref: TRC-PE-Register, extract 2026-06-18 09:11 UTC).

2. Scope and Objectives
The audit scope encompassed systems and processes categorized under the Quantitative Systems domain as defined in the Enterprise Application Inventory (EAI) on 2026-03-29 (EAI Export ID: EAI-2026-QS-029). In scope systems included: QS-Core (APP-QS-001) providing pricing and analytics services; QS-Stream (APP-QS-002) managing ingestion, transformation, and publishing of market and reference data; QS-Calc (APP-QS-003) orchestrating batch/grid computations for end-of-day and intraday risk; QS-UI (APP-QS-004) user-facing tools for scenario configuration; Model Catalog Connector (APP-QS-006) facilitating model registration metadata to MRM repositories; and associated data pipelines and job schedulers declared under the QS domain. Interfaces to Risk Data Warehouse (RDW), Trade Processing Services (TPS), and Regulatory Reporting Extracts (RRE) were reviewed at a control-interface level to validate adequacy of handoffs and accountability boundaries.

Objectives were to: assess the design and operating effectiveness of change and release management across QS; evaluate incident and problem management processes and SLAs; verify access governance, including joiner-mover-leaver and quarterly recertification; review data quality monitoring and lineage documentation for critical data elements (CDEs) within QS-Stream; verify resiliency practices for business-critical components (as defined by Business Impact Analysis, BIA-QS-2026-RevC); and review the interface controls between QE deployments and MRM’s independent model validation lifecycle for relevant code and configuration artifacts. The audit also performed a targeted review of third-party assurance coverage for critical service providers supporting computational workloads and data provisioning.

3. Methodology and Standards
The audit was conducted in accordance with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Standards and the Meridian Capital Internal Audit Methodology (IA-METH-2024-02). Control criteria were mapped to Meridian Technology Risk & Controls (TRC) policies, including SDLC and Change (TRC-SDLC-001), Access Governance (TRC-AG-002), Service Management (TRC-SM-003), Data Governance (EDO-DG-001), and Resilience (TRC-BCP-005). Procedures included document reviews, control walkthroughs, data analytics on ticketing systems, and sample-based testing. A combined sample of 25 normal changes (CHG00348726, CHG00349110, CHG00349603, et al.), 6 emergency changes (CHG-E004412 to CHG-E004417), 20 incidents (INC00295108, INC00295744, et al.), and 6 problems (PRB0004419 to PRB0004424) were examined for conformance to approval workflows, peer review evidencing, release packaging traceability, and post-implementation verification. For access governance, 12 joiner/mover/leaver requests (AR-102949 to AR-102960) and the Q2 recertification attestation (AG-RC-2026-QS, attested 2026-05-07 16:02 UTC) were reviewed for alignment to least-privilege roles and timely attestation. For data quality, 14 active monitors (DQ-QS-Stream-001 to -014) and lineage documentation for five CDEs (CDE-QS-001 PriceSourceID; CDE-QS-004 ValuationDate; CDE-QS-009 RiskBucket; CDE-QS-012 TradeIDRef; CDE-QS-017 CurveFamily) were sampled to validate defined rules, thresholds, stewardship assignments, and incident routing.

Data analytics were performed against exports from ServiceNow (Report ID: SN-EXP-IA-QS-2026-14, extracted 2026-06-10 12:05 UTC) and Jira (Filter: project = QSR and created >= 2025-10-01, export timestamp 2026-06-12 09:52 UTC). No system credentials were requested or used by audit; all access to evidence occurred through read-only enterprise repositories with standard entitlements. Interviews were held with QE, PRE, EDO, and MRM representatives between 2026-04-16 and 2026-06-07 (Interview Log IA-INT-QS-2026, entries IL-034 to IL-061). Consistency checks were executed to reconcile deployment tags with change requests, and to verify closure notes align to testing artifacts and release communications.

4. Governance and Organizational Context
Quantitative Systems are owned by Quantitative Engineering (QE), reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, Markets & Research Technology. Oversight is provided through the Quantitative Systems Steering Committee (QSSC), meeting monthly with representation from QE, PRE, EDO, MRM, Technology Risk & Controls (TRC), and Lines of Business stakeholders from Markets Risk. The QSSC charter (QSSC-CH-2026-01, revised 2026-01-15) defines decision rights for prioritization, release scheduling windows, and acceptance of non-functional requirements. Operating procedures reference enterprise policies for SDLC, change, access, and incident management. Performance reporting is consolidated by PRE into a monthly scorecard (QS-OPS-SCORE-YYYYMM) tracking deployment cadence, mean time to resolution (MTTR), job success rates, and SLA adherence for data delivery.

The audit noted that governance artifacts were current, accessible, and appropriately approved. Meeting minutes and decisions (QSSC-MM-2026-02 through QSSC-MM-2026-06) were filed within two business days of each session and included clear action owner assignments. Interfaces with Model Risk Management are formalized via the Model Deployment Interface Procedure (MRM-QE-IF-2025-07), which separates responsibilities for code lineage, parameter configuration, and independent validation checkpoints. While documentation quality was generally strong, an opportunity exists to further standardize references to data quality monitors within QSSC decision logs to reinforce traceability from business priorities to technical control adjustments (captured as Observation L3 in Section 8).

5. Timeline and Logistics
Planning was initiated on 2026-03-18 (IA Plan ID: IA-PLAN-2026-QS-01). The opening conference was held 2026-04-08 15:00–15:45 UTC (Invitation Ref: IA-MTG-2026-0408-QS), and interim status updates were provided on 2026-05-03 and 2026-05-31. Fieldwork concluded on 2026-06-21 with a preliminary readout to management on 2026-06-25 13:00 UTC. The closing meeting occurred on 2026-07-03 14:30 UTC. Evidence collection windows were communicated and tracked via ServiceNow task group TSK-GRP-IA-QS-2026 (tasks TSK008411 to TSK008468). All evidence items were version-controlled and time-stamped upon receipt. No delays impacted the audit timeline beyond a two-business-day reschedule of the QE capacity planning walkthrough (rebooked from 2026-05-09 to 2026-05-11 due to participant conflicts).

6. System Overview
The Quantitative Systems platform comprises services and pipelines that deliver analytics and curated data to front-office, risk, and finance consumers. Core components include QS-Core (APP-QS-001), an API-driven analytics layer for pricing, sensitivities, and scenario outputs; QS-Stream (APP-QS-002), an ingestion and transformation framework for market and reference data; QS-Calc (APP-QS-003), a batch/grid computation orchestrator supporting end-of-day and intraday cycles; QS-UI (APP-QS-004), presentation tools for scenario configuration and monitoring; and the Model Catalog Connector (APP-QS-006), which synchronizes registration metadata and lifecycle states with MRM repositories. Environments are segregated by lifecycle (Development, Integration, UAT, Production) with standard promotion controls and artifact tagging. Business criticality ratings per BIA-QS-2026-RevC classify QS-Core and QS-Calc as Tier 1 services, QS-Stream as Tier 2, and QS-UI/Connector as Tier 3. Data classification within QS-Stream includes Firm Confidential and Public categories as defined in the Enterprise Data Classification Standard (EDO-CLASS-2024). No sensitive personal data resides in the platform per the Privacy Impact Assessment PIA-QS-2025-01, reaffirmed 2026-02-27.

Integration points with the Risk Data Warehouse (RDW) and Regulatory Reporting Extracts (RRE) follow standardized publish/subscribe patterns with documented schemas and release communications. Operational responsibilities are split between QE (development, release, configuration of models and analytics) and PRE (runtime operations, monitoring, incident coordination). EDO provides stewardship for CDEs flowing through QS-Stream, ensuring data quality rules are cataloged and aligned to enterprise standards. Model Risk Management maintains independence and oversight for model validation and governs the Model Catalog, with defined checkpoints for code artifact identification and deployment readiness.

7. Control Environment Summary
Change and release management processes for QS follow TRC-SDLC-001 and TRC-SM-003. Standard changes require peer review, automated testing evidence, impact assessments, and approval from designated change approvers; emergency changes require post-implementation review within two business days. Observed adherence in sampled changes included traceable links from change requests to deployment tags and regression testing artifacts. Release communications were disseminated through the established channel (DL-QS-Release-Notice) at least 24 hours prior to production implementation, with closures documented in ServiceNow. Access governance aligns to TRC-AG-002 with role-based access mapped to defined entitlements; quarterly recertification was completed for Q2 FY2026 (AG-RC-2026-QS, attested by QE and PRE managers). Service management incorporates incident and problem workflows with SLA tracking, service health dashboards, and retrospective reviews for Sev2 events.

Data governance is anchored by EDO-DG-001 and includes stewardship assignments, lineage documentation, and data quality monitoring. For QS-Stream, rule definitions and thresholds are documented in the Data Quality Catalog (DQ-CAT-QS-Stream, version 2026.05). Operational resilience for Tier 1 services includes documented recovery objectives, runbooks, and scenario testing per TRC-BCP-005. Third-party assurance for critical services is tracked under Vendor Risk Management (VRM) with the latest SOC reports reviewed and mapped to control coverage matrices (VRM-ASSUR-2026-QS).

8. Sampling and Metrics Overview
Samples were selected using stratified criteria to capture peak periods, varied severities, and different deployment windows. The 25 standard changes (e.g., CHG00348726 closed 2026-03-12 21:14 UTC; CHG00349603 closed 2026-04-19 02:46 UTC) evidenced required approvals and test artifacts. Of the 6 emergency changes (CHG-E004413 raised 2026-04-28 04:22 UTC; CHG-E004416 raised 2026-05-17 19:08 UTC), all completed post-implementation reviews within the expected timeframe, with one instance requiring a clarifying addendum added within one business day (CHG-E004416 Addendum Note AN-2026-0519). Incident sampling (20 items; INC00295108 opened 2026-02-09 07:30 UTC; INC00295744 opened 2026-03-01 11:15 UTC) reflected MTTR within target for Sev3 and Sev4, and within extended target for one Sev2 incident due to dependency on a third-party data feed (variance documented in INC00295744 Post-Incident Review PIR-2026-0303). Problem investigations (PRB0004419 to PRB0004424) demonstrated root cause analysis and prevention actions registered in Jira (QSR-7002, QSR-7011).

Access requests sampled (AR-102949 to AR-102960) aligned to least-privilege roles with evidence of manager approval and fulfillment by PRE. The Q2 recertification evidenced timely attestations and removal of two dormant entitlements within five business days of attestation closure (Deprovision tickets TSK008462, TSK008463). Data quality monitors reviewed (DQ-QS-Stream-001 Price Completeness; DQ-QS-Stream-006 Reference ID Conformity; DQ-QS-Stream-014 Timeliness) met defined thresholds in 96.8% of observed daily cycles across the period, with flagged thresholds routed through incident workflows. Vendor assurance artifacts for two critical providers were current (SOC 2 Type II period ending 2025-12-31; review notes VRM-REV-2026-021 and -029 dated 2026-04-22 and 2026-05-16).

Key operational metrics, as presented in the QS-OPS scorecards for 2026-02 through 2026-05, indicate: average monthly deployments to Production of 11.5; emergency change rate at 2.1% of total changes; incident volume averaging 14 per month with Sev2 comprising 7%; Sev2 MTTR median of 2.9 hours; batch job success rate for QS-Calc at 99.2% over the review period; and SLA adherence for data delivery windows at 98.6% for QS-Stream Tier 1 feeds. Variances between the PRE dashboard and QE’s internal tracker for two months were reconciled as reporting boundary differences (included/excluded retry counts). A standardization action has been logged under QSR-7120 to align metric definitions across teams by 2026-09-30.

9. Summary of Preliminary Observations
Two Moderate observations and three Low observations were raised:

- Observation M1: Evidence retention tagging for change-related artifacts is inconsistently applied across Jira Epics QSR-Release-24.03 and QSR-Release-24.04, leading to extended retrieval times. Design remains sound; operating practice requires standardization of references to canonical evidence locations. Management action: Implement evidence-link templates and periodic spot checks (QSR-7096; target 2026-10-15).

- Observation M2: Minor discrepancies in runbook version references between QS-Calc and QS-Stream during two handoffs (Runbook IDs RB-QS-Calc-2026.04 vs RB-QS-Stream-2026.03) were identified in incident closures INC00295744 and INC00296017. While operational impact was contained, alignment of version metadata in closures and dashboards will improve traceability. Management action: Enforce version metadata validation in closure checklist (QSR-7144; target 2026-11-15).

- Observation L1: SLA measurement boundaries differ between PRE dashboard (includes job retries) and QE time-series tracker (excludes retries) for QS-Stream, causing minor variance in reported monthly adherence. Management action: Standardize calculation methodology and glossary (QSR-7120; target 2026-09-30).

- Observation L2: Model deprecation calendar entries were not consistently referenced in two release notes (RN-QS-2026-04B, RN-QS-2026-05A), although MRM records were accurate. Management action: Update release note template to include a model lifecycle section (QSR-7113; target 2026-08-31).

- Observation L3: QSSC decision logs do not consistently cross-reference CDE-level data quality monitors when approving prioritization changes for QS-Stream. Management action: Add CDE/DQ reference fields to QSSC minutes (QSR-7131; target 2026-09-15).

10. Limitations
The audit relied on samples and representations current as of the fieldwork period. Penetration testing and code-level secure development reviews were out of scope and covered by separate assurance functions; results from those functions were not re-performed. The audit did not independently re-execute production changes or replay historical data loads. Conclusions should be interpreted in the context of sampled evidence, observed during the specified timeframe, and may not reflect changes implemented after 2026-06-21.

Follow-up on management action plans will be conducted per Internal Audit procedures, with verification checkpoints scheduled for October and November 2026 (IA-FUP-PLAN-QS-2026, created 2026-07-05 10:22 UTC). No immediate risk escalation is warranted based on current findings.

Internal Audit — Quantitative Systems FY2026
Meridian Capital

Page 3

1. Audit Scope and Objectives
The Internal Audit function conducted a risk-based review of Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (QS) operating environment for Fiscal Year 2026, emphasizing governance, model lifecycle control execution, computational workflow reliability, data handling practices, and incident/change management integration. The scope encompassed end-to-end control activities supporting analytics used by Risk, Treasury, and Finance, including model inventory maintenance, model development and deployment governance, validation closure tracking, data ingestion and transformation quality checks, scheduling and monitoring of batch and intraday processes, and issue/remediation management. User access provisioning and segregation of duties for QS platforms were validated at a high level to confirm coordination with Enterprise Identity & Access Management; a detailed access management evaluation remains subject to a separate audit in FY2026 H2.

Objectives were to (i) assess the design and operating effectiveness of key controls supporting model accuracy, reproducibility, and timeliness; (ii) confirm alignment to internal policies and applicable industry frameworks; (iii) evaluate the completeness and currentness of the QS model inventory and its linkage to validation and performance monitoring records; and (iv) determine whether operational metrics and escalations are consistently captured and reported to governance forums. The period under review was 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30, with certain prior-period artifacts examined to establish control continuity where relevant.

2. Audit Universe and Entities In-Scope
The audit universe included the following QS capabilities and affiliated functions:
- Quantitative Engineering (QE): model build pipelines, packaging, and runtime orchestration; ticket refs QS-2120 through QS-2195.
- Model Risk Management (MRM): policy oversight, independent validation, and performance monitoring attestations; evidence set MRM-EVD-2026-QS-03.
- Risk Analytics Operations (RAO): scheduling, job monitoring, and runbook execution for daily/weekly cycles; ServiceNow assignment group RAO-QSYS.
- Enterprise Data Office (EDO): upstream market/reference data intake stewardship and data quality (DQ) rule maintenance; DQ dashboard reference DQ-RPT-2026-05-31.
- Infrastructure & Reliability (I&R): platform availability SLAs and non-functional observability; change calendar artifact CHG-CAL-Q2FY26.

Systems and services logically associated with QS included the Market Data Normalization service (MDN), Curve Construction Engine (CCE), Scenario Generation Service (SGS), Risk Factor Aggregation (RFA), and the Batch Execution Scheduler (BES). Development and UAT environments were reviewed for promotion controls; Production was reviewed for operational controls, including incident management, change control, and dashboard reporting to senior stakeholders. Third-party vendor feeds were considered only insofar as they intersected with internal DQ controls.

3. Methodology and Standards Applied
The audit applied the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing, with control criteria aligned to COSO 2013 and COBIT 2019 for IT governance, and Meridian’s Model Risk Management Policy (MRM-POL-001) and Model Lifecycle Standard (S-MODEL-014). Fieldwork included control walkthroughs, inspection of artifacts, and targeted re-performance where feasible. Computer-assisted audit techniques were used to analyze control logs and incident/change records exported from ServiceNow and Jira. Population completeness was validated via reconciliations between the QS model inventory (INV-QS-2026-06) and the MRM validation tracker (VAL-TRK-2026-06).

The audit record in Archer GRC is IA-2026-QS-0007. Evidence was stored in SharePoint workspace QSYS_AUDIT_FY26 with subfolders mapped to control domains (e.g., GOV, MLC, DQ, SCH, INC, CHG). Sampling stratification considered control frequency, materiality to financial and risk reporting, and recent change activity density. No testing involved destructive operations; all procedures were observational, documentary, or parallel analytical.

4. Engagement Timeline and Key Milestones
- Planning and risk assessment: 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-18; scoping workshops held with QE, MRM, and RAO on 2026-04-10 (09:00–11:00 UTC) and 2026-04-12 (14:00–16:00 UTC).
- Fieldwork: 2026-04-19 to 2026-06-07, including evidence intake checkpoints on 2026-05-02, 2026-05-16, and 2026-05-30. Notable artifact submissions: SNOW-RITM0025639 (DQ rule catalog export, 2026-05-14T13:47:22Z), QS-2176 (BES scheduler configuration snapshot, 2026-05-21T08:12:05Z), and MRM-EVD-2026-QS-03 (validation closure memos, 2026-05-27T17:41:39Z).
- Reporting and closure: 2026-06-08 to 2026-06-21, with draft observation socialization on 2026-06-15 (Governance Committee pre-read reference GOV-CMT-2026-06-15) and management response consolidation by 2026-06-20.

5. Stakeholder Participation and Roles
The audit team interfaced primarily with:
- Quantitative Engineering: Engineering Lead, Release Coordinator, and QE Controls Analyst.
- Model Risk Management: Head of Validation and Validation Portfolio Lead for QS.
- Risk Analytics Operations: Scheduling Manager and Operations Analysts responsible for daily cycles.
- Enterprise Data Office: Data Steward for Market Data and DQ Product Owner.
- Infrastructure & Reliability: Service Manager for QS platforms and Observability Lead.

Weekly cadence meetings (Tuesdays 15:00–15:45 UTC) were established under invite IA-QS-FY26-CADENCE, with attendance and action items tracked in notes NT-IA-QS-2026-xx. A governance checkpoint with the Quantitative Systems Steering Forum was held on 2026-05-20 (minutes ref QSSF-MIN-2026-05-20), confirming continued sponsorship and availability of resources for evidence collation. Independence and objectivity statements were recorded in Archer entry IA-2026-QS-0007-A1, with no conflicts of interest declared. Management responses to preliminary observations were logged under Jira tickets IAQ-OBS-104 through IAQ-OBS-109 for traceability to remediation owners.

Consistent with the mandate of Internal Audit, the review did not opine on business strategy or model methodology selection but focused on the adequacy and execution of underlying governance and operational controls. No policy exceptions were requested or granted during the engagement window.

Page 4

6. Operating Environment Overview
The Quantitative Systems landscape supports daily, weekly, and ad hoc analytical runs for Market Risk, Counterparty Credit Risk, and Treasury liquidity monitoring. The environment comprises Development, UAT, and Production tiers with a standardized release calendar (primary window Wednesdays 20:00–22:00 UTC; secondary window Saturdays 10:00–12:00 UTC), coordinated through the Enterprise Change Advisory Board. The Batch Execution Scheduler (BES) orchestrates approximately 1,380 jobs on a typical business day, integrating dependencies across the Market Data Normalization (MDN), Curve Construction Engine (CCE), and Scenario Generation Service (SGS). Job-level telemetry feeds an operations dashboard reviewed by RAO at 07:30 UTC and 16:30 UTC, with on-time start and completion serving as key service indicators.

Data inputs are sourced from approved vendor feeds and internal reference repositories overseen by EDO. Data quality controls are applied at intake (schema conformance, timestamp windows) and transformation (key field completeness, continuity checks), with alerts routed to RAO and EDO assignment groups in ServiceNow. QS model artifacts are versioned and cataloged, with traceability from model inventory item to validation pack, deployment ticket, and production run identifier. Production monitoring emphasizes timeliness (SLA: 98.5% of critical jobs complete by 08:15 UTC), stability (critical incident MTTR target ≤ 120 minutes), and reproducibility (ability to re-run with consistent results given identical inputs and configurations).

7. Control Framework Mapping
Internal Audit mapped observed controls to the following domains:
- Governance and Oversight: Steering forum minutes, policy attestations (MRM-POL-001), and quarterly KPI reporting to Risk Technology Governance (RTG). Evidence: GOV-EVD-2026-Q2.
- Model Lifecycle Management: model registration, change classification, validation closure, and performance monitoring. Evidence: INV-QS-2026-06, VAL-TRK-2026-06.
- Change Management: release planning, peer review, pre-implementation checks, and post-implementation verification. Evidence: CHG0057420, CHG0057566, and CAB minutes CAB-MIN-2026-05-08.
- Data Quality: intake and transformation rules, exception handling, and stewardship acknowledgment. Evidence: DQ-RPT-2026-05-31, DQ-RULE-CAT-2026-04.
- Scheduling and Monitoring: job dependency definitions, alert thresholds, and daily sign-offs. Evidence: QS-2176, RAO-DS-2026-05-22.
- Incident and Problem Management: triage procedures, business communication, and root-cause documentation. Evidence: INC0019274, PRB000621.
- Reporting Integrity: reconciliation checks between model outputs and downstream reporting thresholds. Evidence: RPT-REC-2026-06-03.

This mapping aligns to COSO principles (control activities, information and communication, and monitoring activities) and COBIT objectives (BAI06, DSS01, DSS02) tailored to Meridian’s control taxonomy.

8. Sampling Strategy and Evidence Collection
Sampling incorporated both judgmental and random techniques to achieve breadth across domains and depth in high-risk areas:
- Model Lifecycle: 10 models selected from the inventory (risk-classified as High: 4; Medium: 4; Low: 2) to test registration completeness, validation status, and performance monitoring linkages. Inventory IDs: QS-MOD-0143, -0177, -0201, -0225, -0232, -0249, -0260, -0284, -0291, -0303. Associated validation packs: VAL-PCK-2026-0143 et seq.
- Change Management: 25 changes executed between 2026-04-01 and 2026-06-15, covering emergency, standard, and normal categories. Tickets: CHG0057420, CHG0057421, CHG0057488, CHG0057510, CHG0057566, among others; sampling ensured representation of both mid-cycle and maintenance-window deployments.
- Incidents: 15 production incidents affecting QS components during the period, focusing on user-perceived impact, timeliness of triage, and documentation quality. Tickets: INC0019274, INC0019342, INC0019487, INC0019526.
- Data Quality: 30 DQ rule results across MDN and CCE transformations for five business dates per month (April–June). Rule IDs: DQ-MKT-007 (date sequence continuity), DQ-MKT-012 (primary key uniqueness), DQ-REF-003 (instrument attribute completeness).

Exports from ServiceNow and Jira were requested via RITM0025639 on 2026-05-14T13:47:22Z, with a subsequent refresh on 2026-06-10T09:05:18Z. Internal Audit validated sample completeness by reconciling record counts to RAO daily sign-off sheets (RAO-DS-2026-xx) and CAB attendance logs. No population anomalies were identified.

9. Data Sources and Data Quality Observations
Across the sampled period, DQ exception rates for critical MDN fields averaged 0.08%, below the 0.10% operational threshold reported to RTG. Three late-file events were recorded (INC0019487 on 2026-05-17, INC0019526 on 2026-05-24, and INC0019614 on 2026-06-02), all attributable to upstream vendor maintenance notifications. In each case, RAO executed the standard communication protocol to affected stakeholders, and downstream schedules were adjusted within the same processing window; no missed external reporting cutoffs were observed.

Transformation-stage rules DQ-MKT-007 and DQ-MKT-012 flagged sporadic exceptions linked to newly onboarded instruments lacking reference attributes; EDO steward acknowledgments were recorded under TASK0037811 and TASK0037940 with remediation through attribute enrichment on the subsequent business day. 2. Scope and Approach (continued)

2.1 Systems and Processes in Scope
The internal audit encompassed the Quantitative Systems operating landscape as provisioned for FY2026 planning and execution cycles. In scope were the strategic calculation platform (QSTRAT v7.4), the distributed compute grid (RiskGrid-NorthAmerica clusters RG-NA-01 and RG-NA-02), the quantitative job orchestration service (Q-Flow Orchestrator 3.2), the model artifact repository (MLB-Prod Namespace: MLBP-QSYS), and the data acquisition and harmonization tier (DataHub-L3, Environments DH3-PROD and DH3-UAT). The review further considered the integration points between QSTRAT and downstream risk aggregation (RA-Core 5.8) and the nightly data synchronization routines with the enterprise data lake (EDL Zone Z3). Execution management and reference data dependencies were evaluated at the interface level; upstream vendor systems and third-party proprietary schemas remained out of scope, consistent with the risk-based boundary set by the Audit Planning Memorandum APM-QSYS-2026-02, approved 2026-01-19 14:28 UTC.

Business processes evaluated included model deployment gating (from Model Development to Production handoffs), change management (standard and emergency changes executed via Enterprise Change Management Office [ECMO]), incident and problem management (Production Assurance [PA] processes), data lineage documentation and approvals (Data Office governance workflows), and operational monitoring (availability, throughput, and data quality KPIs). Cross-functional controls, such as independent model validation sign-offs (Model Risk & Analytics Validation [MRAV]) and regulatory reporting reconciliations (Regulatory Reporting Operations [RRO]), were assessed insofar as they interacted with Quantitative Systems’ control environment.

2.2 Sampling, Evidence, and IPE Validation
Audit procedures relied on stratified sampling across change, incident, and deployment populations recorded during the period 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31. The sample included 42 standard change tickets (ECMO-CHG series; e.g., CHG00174216, CHG00175604), 7 emergency changes (ECMO-ECHG; e.g., ECHG00004219), 36 model deployment requests (MDR workflow; MDR-2026-0011 to MDR-2026-0056), 28 incidents affecting QSTRAT and RG-NA (ServiceNow INC series; e.g., INC00297214, INC00298903), and 12 problem records (PRB0002316–PRB0002327). Ticket selection was weighted toward criticality (High and Critical priority), production-facing impact, and representation across teams (Quantitative Systems Engineering [QSE], Data Engineering [DE], and Production Assurance [PA]). Evidence was drawn from ServiceNow (Report SN-EXTR-2026-03; extract time 2026-04-03 18:12 UTC), Meridian Git Enterprise (MGE) commit history (Repo IDs: qstrat-core, qflow-scheduler; tag range FY2026.01–FY2026.06), deployment pipeline logs (Orchestrator Event IDs QF-evt-141029 to QF-evt-141983), and the data governance catalog (Collibra instance DGC-Prod, asset lineage IDs LIN-003112, LIN-003457, LIN-003589).

Information Produced by the Entity (IPE) was validated via recalculation and footing checks. For example, deployment throughput metrics reported in QSYS-OPS Dashboard v5.1 were cross-checked against raw pipeline event counts; a variance threshold of 0.5% was applied (actual observed variance: 0.18% over the period). Data quality KPI rollups (DQ-KPI-Set-7) were re-performed on independent extracts from DH3-PROD object stores (S3-compatible namespace dh3p-l3-qsys) to confirm completeness and null-rate computations. Audit working papers reference these validations under AUR-2026-017, sections AUR17-2.2.1 to AUR17-2.2.5. Time stamps were retained for all evidence captures; for instance, MDR-2026-0037 sign-off retrieval occurred 2026-03-08 09:47 EST, confirmed via ServiceNow audit trail EventID SN-AUD-773512.

2.3 Scope Limitations and Exclusions
Certain non-material geographies (APAC development sandboxes and EMEA prototype clusters) remained out of scope per risk assessment RAT-QSYS-2026-01, given immaterial transaction volumes and the absence of production connectivity. Vendor-managed market data plant configurations were assessed only at the consumption interface and SLA reporting layers; vendor-side internal controls were not tested. Analytics notebooks executed in user-specific research spaces (ResearchLab-RL2) were excluded unless they formed part of an MDR-documented production candidate. No alternative procedures were required for the excluded items; management concurrence was documented in MGT-ACK-2026-12, signed by the Head of Quantitative Systems on 2026-01-23 11:05 UTC.

2.4 Key Metrics and Control Objectives Reviewed
The audit assessed adherence to defined control objectives across availability, change governance, and data quality:

- Availability and Performance: Target ≥ 99.5% monthly service availability for QSTRAT and RG-NA; job success ratio ≥ 98.0%; 95th percentile job completion time within ±10% of baseline (baseline established FY2025Q4).
- Change Governance: 100% of standard changes with approved risk/impact assessment and back-out plan attached pre-implementation; emergency changes ratified within two business days; segregation of duties enforced between code authors and approvers in MGE.
- Data Quality and Lineage: ≥ 99.0% feed completeness for in-scope market and reference data sets; timeliness within contractual SLAs; lineage documentation current and approved for all critical data elements (CDEs) consumed by QSTRAT.

Observed results for the audit period showed QSTRAT availability at 99.87% (excluding a 17-minute planned maintenance window, CHG00175110), RG-NA job success at 98.6%, and 95th percentile completion time within 7.9% of baseline. Change governance compliance was strong: 41 of 42 standard changes contained complete documentation; one variance (CHG00175604) initially lacked a finalized back-out plan, subsequently remediated prior to deployment (ticket updated 2026-02-14 15:37:12 UTC). All seven emergency changes were post-facto ratified within the two-business-day requirement (average 0.8 days). Data quality measures indicated 99.2% average feed completeness across five key data sets (MD-Core, RF-Static, FX-Spot, SecMaster-L3, and Calendar-Holiday), with three isolated timeliness deviations discussed in Section 4.

No evidence of management override of established controls was identified. Sample sizes produced a 90% confidence level with an estimated ±7% margin of error for change ticket attribute testing; residual sampling risk is disclosed in AUR17-Appendix-B. All conclusions are based on evidence obtained as of 2026-04-12 and do not reflect subsequent operational changes.

Control families assessed included completeness, timeliness, validity, and reconciliation checks embedded within DH3-PROD ingest pipelines and QSTRAT pre-ingest guards. Daily feed count reconciliation between vendor delivery manifests and DH3 object store receipts showed ≥ 99.0% completeness for the period, with a monthly average of 99.2%. Timeliness controls enforced SLA windows of T+0 for intraday market data and T+1 for static reference data. Three isolated timeliness deviations were recorded:
- INC00298347 (2026-03-12 09:14 ET): MD-Core equities snapshot arrived 17 minutes past SLA due to vendor-side network congestion. No downstream calculation breaches occurred; Q-Flow auto-scheduled a re-run within the buffer window (Event QF-evt-141612).

Validity checks (schema conformance, permissible value ranges) and referential integrity checks (symbol-to-identifier concordance) operated as designed. Sampled exceptions were traceable to root causes and closed via Problem Records PRB0002319 and PRB0002321 with corrective actions focusing on vendor notification thresholds and internal monitoring thresholds calibration. Monthly data quality KPI summaries (DQ-KPI-Set-7) indicated null rates in key numeric fields at 0.03% (target ≤ 0.10%) and duplicate detection rates at 0.004% (target ≤ 0.05%), reflecting sustained control effectiveness.

4.3 Reconciliations and Downstream Consistency
Reconciliation procedures between QSTRAT pre-calculation aggregates and RA-Core post-calculation aggregates were reviewed for five randomly selected business dates across the period. Tolerances of ±5 basis points for aggregate risk deltas and gamma exposure rollups were met in all cases. Two immaterial variances were observed in commodity exposure rollups on 2026-03-04 and 2026-03-18, attributable to instrument late classifications subsequently corrected in SecMaster-L3 (CHG00175892). Evidence of reconciliation review and sign-off was present in RA-Core control logs (RC-LOG-2026-03-04 20:11 UTC; RC-LOG-2026-03-18 20:09 UTC) and mirrored in QSYS-OPS daily checklists (OPS-CHK-2026-063, OPS-CHK-2026-077).

4.4 Observations and Minor Improvements
Overall, governance over data sourcing and lineage is mature and consistently applied. Two minor enhancements are noted for management attention: (1) prompt completion of lineage certification post-schema change to minimize “Pending Approval” durations (RF-Static was pending for 7 business days), and (2) alignment of data classification tags between DH3-PROD and the DGC catalog for three child attributes under SecMaster-L3, which currently show “Internal” in DH3 and “Confidential – Internal Use” in DGC (tracking item DGC-TKT-2026-0097, owner: Data Steward—SecMaster; target 2026-05-10). These observations do not rise to the level of findings but, if addressed, would further streamline attestations tied to MDR workflows.

No systemic deficiencies were identified in the data sourcing and lineage control environment during the period under review.

Asset-level lineage in Atlas correctly reflected vendor sources, intermediate transformations, and consuming applications (QRM-VaR, QRM-Stress, and QS-Analytics), including partitioning and enrichment steps. We observed consistent use of authoritative keys (instr_id, source_id) and timestamp attributes to ensure traceability. The visual lineage matched the operational flow as observed in Airflow runs for sampled dates, with no orphaned or ambiguous nodes. Minor variances in attribute naming conventions between the Atlas glossary and physical schema (e.g., “px_close” vs. “close_price”) were tracked under QSYS-2219 and scheduled for harmonization under CHG0011511 (deployed 2026-03-22 03:06 UTC with eCAB approval eCAB-2026-21).

Schema drift and data quality alerts were functioning as intended. During the period, four low-severity schema drift alerts were raised (ELO alert refs: ALERT-ELK-2026-1198, -1201, -1223, -1254) due to a vendor adding an optional commentary field to the FX feed and extending attribute length for an equity venue code. These changes were backward-compatible; no consumer impact was noted. Closeout activities included updating the schema registry documentation and performing regression checks (JIRA DE-MP-1447; release CHG0011488 on 2026-03-15 01:41 UTC). Audit review confirmed evidence of peer review and sign-off by QS Ops (approver: T. Nguyen, timestamp 2026-03-14 18:19 EST).

The deduplication and late-arrival logic operated within tolerance. A 90-day reconciliation sample (n=12 checkpoints) indicated average record variance of 0.03% between landing and curated layers, attributable to late-day vendor retransmissions near the UTC date boundary. The largest single-day variance (0.07% on 2026-02-06) was analyzed under incident MC-QS-INC-2026-0413 (opened 2026-02-06 21:03 UTC; resolved 2026-02-07 02:28 UTC). Root cause was a retransmit window overlap for Asia-Pacific equity markets coinciding with a maintenance restart at a downstream consumer. Mitigation included tightening the acceptance window by 2 minutes for the affected venue and adding post-curation reconciliation logs. No data loss or mispricing was observed; QRM consumers processed the corrected batch within the same operations cycle.

Staleness SLA adherence remained strong. For Level-1 FX and equity feeds, freshness compliance was 98.7% within the defined ≤15-minute SLA at point of consumption. Non-compliant intervals clustered around 2026-03-08 07:00–08:00 UTC during the Daylight Saving Time transition and a vendor-side heartbeat delay (vendor advisory REF-2026-031; QS Ops ticket QSYS-2184). The QS Ops bridge documented appropriate notification and monitoring posture; no downstream breaches of trading or risk calculation windows occurred. The audit corroborated that alerts reached on-call personnel within one minute of breach and that incident timelines were logged in Servicenow (INC0019283, opened 2026-03-08 07:06 UTC; resolved 08:02 UTC).

Reference data controls for symbology and currency mapping were satisfactory with a noted improvement action. We observed an isolated inconsistency where London Stock Exchange secondary listings were normalized to an obsolete internal venue code in the REF-SECMASTER mapping layer. The issue was detected by the monthly symbol health check (report QS-REF-HEALTH-2026-02, run 2026-02-20 10:00 UTC) and remediated via MAP-SYM-2026.02 uplift (CHG0011423, implemented 2026-03-11 21:04 UTC). The potential impact was limited to a non-critical exposure report that reads venue-level attributes; no valuation or risk metrics were affected. Management has committed to extending the symbol normalization regression suite to include venue code backfills for cross-listed instruments (action item QSYS-ACT-2026-011, due 2026-05-15; status: In Progress, 60% complete as of 2026-04-01 12:30 EST).

Retention and recovery controls conformed to policy. Sampled data restore tests from cold archive for MD-IR-CRV (request RST-2026-0031; executed 2026-03-05 13:22 UTC) completed within the targeted recovery time objective. Audit confirmed evidence of chain-of-custody logging for restored artifacts and timely data destruction post-validation.

Conclusion. Overall, data lineage and quality controls for market and reference data are effective. Documentation is current, alerting is appropriately tuned, and remediation workflows are timely. Minor enhancement opportunities exist in glossary-to-schema naming harmonization and expansion of symbol normalization regression coverage. These items do not materially affect control effectiveness and are actively tracked with clear owners and due dates.

4.3 Model Performance Monitoring — Backtesting and Stability

Scope and monitoring framework. The audit assessed the design and operating effectiveness of model performance monitoring across key QSYS models: Value-at-Risk (QRM-VAR-SR02), Stress Testing (QRM-STRESS-CRD), and an alpha generation module for systematic strategies (QRM-VAOG-AlphaV3). We reviewed backtesting results, PnL attribution coverage, alert thresholds, and governance workflows with Model Risk & Validation (MRV) and Quantitative Systems Operations (QS Ops) for the period 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31. Evidence included monitoring dashboards (QS Monitor v4.6; board QRM-MON-Board-12), MRV validation reports (MRV-VAL-2026-0041, issued 2026-02-28), and incident/problem tickets (INC0019551, PRB000472).

Backtesting results were within tolerance. The rolling 252-trading-day VaR backtest showed nine exceptions as of 2026-03-31, below the yellow threshold and consistent with the model’s risk appetite. Two exceptions fell within the audit window (2026-01-12 and 2026-03-14), coincident with outsized moves in rates and FX, respectively. MRV independently reviewed both exceptions (MRV-EXC-2026-0007, -0010) and confirmed alignment with market conditions, with no indication of model misspecification or data issues. Stress testing scenario coverage was expanded during the period to include a commodities shock vector (CHG0011537; eCAB-2026-22) per prior year recommendations; monitoring thresholds were recalibrated accordingly, and no false positives were introduced.

PnL explain and attribution coverage exceeded targets. For Q1 FY2026, daily PnL attribution coverage averaged 97.8% (target ≥95%), with residuals primarily linked to fees and execution slippage outside model scope. Exceptions were tracked under QSYS-2209 and closed with documentation by QS Analytics on 2026-03-19 16:44 EST. The monitoring platform flagged an elevated residual on 2026-02-22 (ALRT-QRM-2026-0312); investigation (INC0019462) traced the variance to a delayed dividend adjustment ingestion. DE-MP confirmed correction in the subsequent batch; no recurrences observed.

Model drift and stability indicators were adequately instrumented. For QRM-VAOG-AlphaV3, feature distribution drift indices ranged 0.92–1.05 during the review period, within the established control limits. A transient drift alert on 2026-01-19 14:08 UTC (ALRT-QRM-2026-0201) was escalated to MRV (ticket MRV-VAL-2026-0041) and resolved as non-material, stemming from a rebalancing-induced shift in factor exposures. The VaR computational pipeline met latency SLOs (p99 ≤480 seconds) except for two days (2026-03-03, 2026-03-09) when upstream batch durations extended following permitted platform changes (CHG0011589). Governance and re-approval. The VaR model (QRM-VAR-SR02) completed timely periodic re-approval on 2026-02-28 with conditions to evaluate an expanded stress window for select asset classes by mid-year (MRV condition set MRV-CND-2026-12). The action plan (QSYS-ACT-2026-017) designates joint ownership between MRV and QSYS for implementation and measurement, with interim checkpoints scheduled (2026-04-30 and 2026-06-15). As of 2026-04-01 09:55 EST, the plan is on track (45% complete), with preliminary scenario backfill completed and calibration testing underway (JIRA QRM-TEST-329).

Conclusion. Monitoring controls for model performance, drift, and backtesting are effective. Alerts are calibrated to business risk, responses are timely, and documentation supports traceability. The SLO variances observed were attributable to approved upstream changes and were managed without customer or regulatory impact.

4.4 Change Management — Release Cadence and Control Effectiveness

Scope and population. We evaluated releases affecting the QSYS production estate (applications: QRM-VaR, QRM-Stress, QS-Analytics; platforms: QSYS-Core, Data Ingestion) executed from 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-31. The audit tested 30 changes from a population of 184 production changes (ServiceNow CHG population extract SNAP-CHG-QSYS-2026Q1, generated 2026-04-02 08:12 EST), covering standard, normal, and emergency categories.

Cadence and approvals. Normal changes followed the defined Tuesday/Thursday 20:00–23:00 ET windows with eCAB approvals recorded under eCAB-2026-07, -14, -21. Change records consistently contained business justification, risk assessments, and backout plans. Segregation of duties was effective: in all tested samples, developers and approvers were distinct, with approvals from authorized roles (Technology Risk Office, Production Assurance). Build artifacts were appropriately referenced (Jenkins job QS-CI-Release build #982, completed 2026-02-18 01:12 UTC), and pre-implementation testing evidence was present for 29/30 sampled changes (96.7%). The exception (CHG0011607) lacked an attached functional test summary at approval time; the artifact was subsequently uploaded (2026-02-19 10:22 EST) with eCAB notation and no adverse outcomes.

Execution quality and post-implementation review. Change failure rate for the quarter was 0.6% (1 of 184), with a single change rolled back due to a validation query error in a non-critical reporting job (CHG0011554; associated incident INC0019520 opened 2026-03-05 00:37 UTC; resolved 03:41 UTC). Emergency changes (n=3: CHG0011734, CHG0011798, CHG0011831) were appropriately invoked in response to vendor-side anomalies and executed under expedited approvals, followed by mandatory retrospectives documented by Production Assurance (PA-SO-2026-0252, -0261, -0267). All three retrospectives identified clear preventive actions, which were tracked to closure in JIRA (QSYS-2231, QSYS-2237, DE-MP-1479).

Control evidence and linkage to operational stability. Post-implementation monitoring evidence (30–60 minute observation logs with sign-offs) was present in 100% of sampled standard/normal changes. Where incidents occurred within 24 hours of change (n=4; INC0019459, INC0019481, INC0019520, INC0019568), mean time to resolve was 3.2 hours, and root cause attribution was completed within two business days in each case. None of the incidents led to missed reporting deadlines or incomplete risk runs, and two were traced to external dependencies (vendor feed delays) rather than release defects. The change calendar reflected appropriate blackout observance around month-end risk cycles.

Process maturity and data quality of the change register. The change register was complete and timely, with accurate linkages to impacted configuration items and downstream applications. Minor inconsistencies were noted in the naming convention of deployment packages across QSYS-Core and Data Ingestion (e.g., QS-PLAT-2026.3.14 vs. QS-PLATFORM-2026_03_14), which can hinder automated reporting. Management has initiated a standardization exercise (QSYS-OPS-STD-2026-05) with a target effective date of 2026-06-30. Additionally, the free-text “success/failure rationale” field was sparsely populated in 5 of 30 sampled records; while evidence existed elsewhere, completing this field would strengthen auditability.

Conclusion and rating. Change management controls are effective. Approvals are timely, segregation of duties is maintained, and execution quality is high with a low failure rate. Minor enhancements to artifact attachment discipline and naming standardization are underway and, in our assessment, do not materially impact control effectiveness. Management has accepted the observations with remediation dates aligned to Q3 FY2026 and designated accountable owners within QS Ops and DE-MP.

Section 6: Data Governance and Lineage Controls

6.1 Overview and Scope
For FY2026, the Internal Audit function evaluated Meridian Capital’s data governance implementation supporting Quantitative Systems (QSYS) with a focus on market, reference, and derived datasets that serve pricing models, intraday risk analytics, and end-of-day valuations. The assessment encompassed lineage registration, data quality controls, exception management workflows, and archival/retention conformance. Evidence was obtained via repository extracts from the enterprise data catalog (Atlas v3.9), control attestations filed by Data Governance Office (DGO) and Quant Platform Engineering (QPE), and targeted sampling of data pipelines supporting datasets DS-MKTD-0012 (equities consolidated tape), DS-FXSP-0041 (spot FX intraday), and DS-REFD-0090 (security master reference clusters), with corroboration against ServiceNow and Jira tickets logged between 2025-10-01 and 2026-05-31.

6.2 Data Sourcing and Lineage Registration
Primary and contingent sourcing paths for each in-scope dataset are registered in the enterprise catalog with upstream provider identifiers, normalization stages, and consumer mappings to model families QMOD-EQ-PRC-Alpha and QMOD-FX-Vol-SV. Lineage coverage across the QSYS domain improved from 91% (FY2025) to 96% (FY2026 YTD) based on control DGO-LNG-004 scorecards (report DGO-Score-2026Q2, 2026-05-27 13:14Z). The residual 4% pertains to intraday OTC quote enrichments aggregated by Market Data Operations (MDO) for select fixed income instruments where limited metadata is passed through ad hoc staging. This gap is documented (ticket DGO-1637, opened 2026-03-06 10:22Z) with remediation in progress to harmonize enrichment steps and register full upstream identifiers; target status is “On Track” with a forecast close of 2026-08-31 pending UAT by QPE.

Lineage paths include explicit stage identifiers (STG-QSYS-ING, NRM-QSYS-STD, CRT-QSYS-DER) and completion timestamps. Audit sampling validated that consumer mappings reflect actual dependencies observed in Airflow run histories for 28 out of 30 sampled jobs; two mappings (Airflow DAG IDs qsys_fx_spot_norm_v2, qsys_eq_adjclose_roll_v4) still reference deprecated consumers in non-production only; a cleanup task (QSYS-28401) has been filed with no downstream risk declared.

6.3 Data Quality Controls and Exception Handling
Quality checks across ingestion and normalization include field-level null thresholds, schema compatibility checks, and cross-provider reconciliation counts implemented under control set QPE-QC-07 to QPE-QC-14. For DS-FXSP-0041, reconciliations against provider day-close totals (QC-11) showed 99.8% pass rate over the period, with four amber events in February 2026 relating to provider maintenance windows (ServiceNow INC0019453 opened 2026-02-14 07:28Z; resolved 2026-02-14 10:16Z; MTTR 2h48m). Exception handling follows documented runbook references in the Quality Incident Register (QIR) with automated ticket creation for red threshold breaches and batch rechecks at T+15 minutes for transient vendor gaps. No critical red breaches were recorded for QSYS during Q2 FY2026.

Schema drift detection (QC-12) flagged one change on 2026-02-05 07:12Z for a new optional field introduced by the alternate market data provider within equities corporate action feeds. The alert was triaged within 12 minutes by MDO (ticket MDO-CA-7713) and normalized in the staging layer following standard governance review (Change CHG0017761 approved 2026-02-05 08:03Z, CAB reference CAB-2026-W05-QSYS). No consumer impact was observed; downstream models treated the new attribute as non-material pending prioritization by the Quant Research Council (QRC).

For DS-REFD-0090, attribute completeness checkpoints (QC-09) over security master clusters achieved a 99.2% completeness score, down modestly from 99.4% in FY2025, primarily due to delayed LEI refreshes for newly listed small-cap issuers (MDO backlog report MDO-REF-Rep-2026Q2). The Data Governance Office flagged the trend as within tolerance but recommended continued weekly monitoring; QPE’s response plan and tracking (QSYS-28917) indicate corrective actions are underway with MDO to align refresh cadence with listing surges during earnings seasons.

6.4 Data Timeliness and SLAs
Timeliness adherence for ingestion and normalization phases against published SLAs (POL-DATA-SLA-06) was measured across 1,482 batch instances. SLA attainment averaged 99.3% across trading days, with nine instances of minor lateness (<7 minutes) during daylight saving transitions in March 2026. These were pre-communicated by Enterprise Scheduling Services (ESS) (Advisory ESS-ADV-2026-03-07) and tracked as known events. No downstream model recalculation windows were breached; capacity buffers absorbed the delays, and operational metrics remained green in the QSYS Command Center dashboard for the relevant days.

6.5 Retention, Archival, and Disposal
Retention and archival practices for raw ticks, normalized snapshots, and derived aggregates were reviewed against policy POL-DATA-RET-09 and procedure DGO-PRO-RET-04. Raw ticks for DS-MKTD-0012 are retained for 13 months in warm storage with quarterly certified archives to compliant cold storage tiers; normalized snapshots are held for 36 months; derived aggregates for 60 months. Compliance for Q1–Q3 FY2026 was 100% based on storage certification attestations (STOR-ATT-2026Q3). In Q4 FY2026 to date, one variance was recorded: the March 2026 quarterly archive for DS-FXSP-0041 completed with a 48-hour delay due to a capacity rebalancing event within the cold tier (ticket STOR-2298 opened 2026-04-02 02:11Z, closed 2026-04-04 04:29Z). No data loss or integrity issues were identified; the event remained within the grace period contemplated by the policy and was communicated via standard variance reporting to DGO.

6.6 Quality Scorecards and Governance Reporting
Monthly data quality scorecards (DGO-SC-2026-01 to -05) show consistent performance within thresholds: weighted composite scores of 4.5/5 for FX spot and 4.1/5 for equities consolidated tape, versus a minimum acceptable composite of 4.0/5 per QSYS standards. Trend analysis highlights stable reconciliation rates and improved null-handling in security master clusters following attribute normalization deployed in January 2026 (Change CHG0017029, implemented 2026-01-19 21:47Z). Governance reporting to the Model Oversight and Review Committee (MORC) includes a quarterly lineage coverage update and a listing of open data-related corrective actions. As of 2026-05-31, three corrective actions remain open for the QSYS domain (DGO-1637; QSYS-28917; MDO-CA-7713), all categorized as low to moderate operational impact with established target closure timelines and identified accountable owners.

Section 7: Change Management, Model Governance, and Operational Monitoring

7.1 Change Management and Release Governance
Internal Audit reviewed QSYS change and release practices across application code, model parameter sets, and data transformation logic for the period 2025-10-01 to 2026-05-31. Evidence was drawn from ServiceNow Change records (CHG0016684–CHG0018129), Jira epics and stories (e.g., QSYS-Rel-Q2.3.17; QSYS-28401; QSYS-29103), and CAB minutes (CAB-2026-W07-QSYS through CAB-2026-W21-QSYS). The release cadence remained biweekly for non-critical updates, with documented freeze windows around quarter-ends. Segregation of duties was consistently observed: 100% of sampled production changes (n=42) had peer code review recorded by a team member not involved in the originating development (reviewers from QPE-Pricing Core and QPE-Data Services), and 100% had explicit approvals from Change Owners and CAB delegates.

Approval timeliness across standard changes met internal targets in 92% of cases; three changes experienced approval lag exceeding four hours due to multi-region sign-off coordination (CHG0017792, CHG0017831, CHG0018045). These were pre-classified as low-risk parameter refreshes and executed within the same business day. Two emergency changes were logged during the period (CHG-E001122, 2026-03-18 12:34Z; CHG-E001137, 2026-04-26 06:51Z) to accommodate a non-disruptive vendor field label update and a minor compatibility patch within a normalization routine. Both were pre-authorized under established emergency criteria and followed with post-implementation reviews (PIR) within 48 hours.

Automated validation coverage improved: unit test coverage for core pricing libraries increased from 78% to 84% per Q1–Q2 trend reports (QPE-QA-Rep-2026Q2). Pipeline regression checks for data transforms recorded a 99.2% pass rate, with transient failures linked to provider-side test endpoints during off-market hours. No deviations from documented deployment steps were observed in the sample, and rollback verification entries were present for all sampled changes.

7.2 Model Governance and Oversight
Model lifecycle controls for the QSYS domain align with Meridian Capital’s Model Risk Management Standard (MRM-STD-2024-R2). Audit testing covered model registration, validation attestations, periodic performance reviews, and ongoing monitoring operated by the Quant Risk Analytics (QRA) team. During the period, one new model version, QMOD-FX-Vol-SV v4.5, entered controlled production on 2026-04-12 21:47Z following MORC endorsement (MORC-Min-2026-04-08). Validation artifacts (QRA-VAL-2026-014) included challenger–champion analyses, sensitivity testing summaries, and implementation verification signed by QPE. All required sign-offs were obtained, including Data Governance confirmation on input suitability (DGO-CFM-2026-031) and Legal/Compliance acknowledgment of use case alignment.

Backtesting results for QMOD-EQ-PRC-Alpha over the trailing six months were reported to MORC with tracking identifiers QRA-BKT-2026-002 through -005. Performance remained within pre-established tolerances; two amber signals were recorded in January and April 2026 related to elevated dispersion during earnings weeks. MORC recorded no actions beyond continued monitoring given the transient and contextually explained deviations.

7.3 Operational Monitoring and Alert Handling
QSYS operational monitoring covers data receipt timing, transform completion, model scoring latency, and downstream publish confirmation. Alerts are classified into informational, amber, and red, with route rules to the QSYS Command Center (QCC) staffed by QPE operations analysts, 06:00–22:00 local market coverage with on-call rotation thereafter. Over the review window, 5,412 alerts were logged: 92.6% informational, 6.8% amber, and 0.6% red. No red alerts required MORC escalation. Five amber alerts (INC0019726, INC0019881, INC0020119, INC0020440, INC0020574) were selected for detailed review. Root causes included: delayed corporate action downstream confirmation during peak filings (two cases), stale vendor flags on an alternate FX feed (one case), and recalibration run queueing during a maintenance window (two cases). Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for the sample averaged 14 minutes; mean time to resolve (MTTR) 3.6 hours. All incidents had complete notes, clear ownership transitions, and cross-references to related problems where applicable.

7.4 Incident and Problem Management
Internal Audit examined 30 incident tickets and 8 problem records associated with QSYS during the period. Service availability during defined trading hours was 99.95%, with two partial degradations on 2026-03-11 and 2026-05-02 attributable to extended batch windows intersecting pre-open health checks. Neither event resulted in missed valuation cutoffs or client reporting impacts. Post-incident reviews were completed within five business days in 100% of cases, with captured actions centered on runbook clarification, provider communication enhancements, and scheduling annotations for known cyclical volume spikes. Problem investigations (PRB000317, PRB000322) consolidated recurring low-severity alerts into a single thematic review addressing seasonal corporate action throughput; both remain open with monthly status to MORC and target closure in 2026-07.

Capacity metrics indicate stable headroom. Average model scoring latency at the 95th percentile was 1.8 seconds for equities and 1.2 seconds for FX workloads, within the defined thresholds. Documentation hygiene across runbooks, control descriptions, and model documentation showed measurable improvement. Of the 56 artifacts sampled, 55 were current to within 90 days, and one runbook (RB-QSYS-FX-Intraday v3.2) was updated during fieldwork to reflect revised alert taxonomies (commit QPE-Docs-2026-05-21 16:03Z). Evidence retention for change approvals, validation attestations, and PIRs was complete, with traceability across systems using consistent identifiers. Quarterly attestations by control owners (QPE, DGO, MDO) were filed timely and matched operational practices observed.

Overall, the control environment supporting QSYS change management, model governance, and operational monitoring is functioning effectively, with minor timing variances and documentation updates tracked through standard processes. Management has acknowledged the open corrective actions and has provided target dates and accountable owners. No high-severity findings were raised for the period under review.

Section 5: Technology Change, Release, and Configuration Management

5.1 Change and Release Management — Design and Operating Effectiveness

Audit procedures covered the end-to-end governance of application and analytics changes across the Quantitative Systems (QS) estate, including code repositories, orchestration layers, data transformation pipelines, and analytical model packages. The audit evaluated adherence to Meridian Capital’s SDLC Standard SD-14 (rev. 2025.4) and the Enterprise Change Management Policy CMP-001 (rev. 2026.1). The assessment focused on design adequacy of controls, operating effectiveness during FY2026 (Q1–Q3), and alignment with risk appetite statements overseen by the Model Governance Office (MGO). We performed walkthroughs with Quant Platform Engineering (QPE), Production Operations (ProdOps), and the Enterprise Release Management Office (ERMO); inspected artifacts in Jira (Project key: QSYS), ServiceNow Change (CHG), and Confluence; and conducted sample-based testing of 32 production changes (population: 611 changes, 2025-10-01 to 2026-06-30). Sampling targeted standard changes (n=12), normal changes (n=16), and emergency changes (n=4), with coverage across model deployment, batch orchestration, and data schema evolution.

Control design is assessed as sound. The QS Deployment Framework (QSDF v3.6) enforces gate checks comprising peer code review (two-person approval minimum), automated unit and regression test execution, artifact signing, and segregation of duties between developers and release approvers. Promotion paths (DEV → QA → UAT → PRD) are consistently documented in the release record with environment-specific validation steps and rollback criteria. A weekly Change Advisory Board (CAB) convened by ERMO (Tuesdays, 14:00–14:45 ET) documents risk, impact, and scheduling decisions; minutes are cataloged under MC-QS-CAB-2026-xx. The QS-specific release calendar (ref. RELCAL-QS-2026) delineates cut-off windows and blackout periods coordinated with downstream finance close cycles.

Operating effectiveness is rated satisfactory with minor opportunities for standardization. Of the 32 sampled changes, 31 (96.9%) had complete pre-implementation approvals captured in ServiceNow prior to deployment time; one change (CHG-2026-2198, implemented 2026-04-19 22:17 UTC) exhibited an approval timestamp recorded 7 minutes post-deployment due to a documented workflow latency. Subsequent investigation (Problem ticket PRB-2026-0098) confirmed the approval had been granted contemporaneously via CAB consent (minutes MC-QS-CAB-0419) and that the record sync deferred the write-back. All changes evidenced peer review (GitLab MR approvals: dual sign-off), with test pipelines executed successfully (pipeline refs: GL-P-87412 through GL-P-87443). Emergency changes (n=4) followed the designated post-implementation review path within 48 hours, with PIR attachments present (PIR-2026-EM-003, -006, -009, -011) and explicit validation of stability across the following batch cycle.

We observed consistent use of implementation plans and backout descriptions. However, content quality varied in specificity for batch orchestration changes. Three records (CHG-2026-2031, CHG-2026-2147, CHG-2026-2450) referenced generic rollback notes without cross-referencing the precise DAG identifiers and pause criteria documented in the QS Orchestration Catalogue (QORC-Index). While not impeding safe execution, ERMO agreed that a standardized rollback narrative template would enhance clarity and reduce interpretive variability for the overnight ProdOps team. An enhancement request (RFE-2026-0119) was logged on 2026-06-12 to revise the change form and add mandatory fields for orchestration asset IDs and validation probes.

We re-performed linkage testing for traceability from business requirement to deployment artifact for nine sampled changes. Each had a Jira user story or epic with acceptance criteria, evidence of UAT sign-off (RAT and DSO stakeholders), and traceable build hashes in the release ticket. Notably, the model recalibration release QSYS-EPIC-3821 (deployed 2026-05-03 01:12 UTC; CHG-2026-2344) demonstrated exemplary traceability, including attached model validation memos (MGO-VAL-2026-052, 2026-04-26) and a production verification plan with pre/post key performance indicator snapshots.

Forward-fix handling for two minor defects introduced in release wave 2026.06 (INC-2026-07482, INC-2026-07511) adhered to the emergency path with controlled scope and documented risk acceptance by the QS Service Owner (QS-SO-01). No evidence of developer self-approval was observed; approvers were from separate teams and roles per CMP-001. Release deferrals due to fiscal close blackout were appropriately rescheduled with customer communication records present (COMM-2026-CLS-07).

Conclusion: Controls are designed appropriately and operate effectively. We rate this area Low residual risk. Management has initiated process enhancements (RFE-2026-0119) to standardize rollback documentation for orchestration assets. Target completion: 2026-09-30. Responsible: ERMO in partnership with ProdOps and QPE.

5.2 Configuration Management and Baseline Integrity

We assessed configuration governance for QS compute, storage, orchestration, and analytics runtimes to determine whether assets are inventoried, baselined, and monitored for unauthorized drift. The scope included configuration items (CIs) in the Enterprise CMDB tagged with Service: Quantitative Systems (ServiceNow filter: svc=QS, status=Active), associated code-based configuration repositories, and parameter sets referenced by the orchestration layer.

Inventory completeness is materially adequate. As of 2026-06-30, 1,284 CIs are registered under QS, comprising application services (n=214), batch workflows (logical CIs; n=411), data domains (n=93), and platform nodes/containers (n=566). Coverage for production CIs is 98.9% based on reconciliation with QPE’s internal deployment registry (QREG-2026-Q2), with four logical workflows identified as deployed but not yet reflected as discrete CMDB entries (Remediation task CMDB-2026-144). Non-production coverage is 96.2% and improving per the quarterly campaign led by the Data Strategy Office (DSO).

Baseline standards are defined in Configuration Standard CS-07 and QS-Specific Parameter Baseline QPBL-2026. Golden configurations are versioned in Git with change history. We validated baseline alignment for a random sample of 25 production CIs. Root cause categorizations for the full population concentrate in four domains: upstream dependency latency (31%), orchestration dependency configuration defects (18%), data quality rule triggers resulting in protective halts (17%), and environment resource contention (12%). The remaining 22% were single-occurrence operational anomalies (e.g., scheduling deferrals during fiscal close, ad hoc remediation of malformed input files). Communication to stakeholders met timeliness targets. Incident bridges were opened promptly for Sev1/Sev2 events, and summary updates were disseminated at intervals aligned to severity. The audit assessed whether QS has appropriate mechanisms to monitor, analyze, and forecast performance and capacity to meet service level objectives. Scope and Objectives
The audit assessed data quality and lineage controls across Meridian Capital’s Quantitative Systems (QSYS) for FY2026 (period: 01 Jul 2025 through 30 Jun 2026), focusing on front-to-risk market data pipelines, pricing reference datasets, risk factor timeseries, and trade/position enrichment flows stewarded by Risk Data Services (RDS) and the Quantitative Engineering (QE) organization. Procedures included: (a) sampling 28 business-critical data elements across seven pipelines (sample count: n=420 data records per element spanning five business days per quarter), (b) review of lineage capture in the Enterprise Data Governance Catalog (DGC) for selected elements, (c) reconciliation of control totals between source and consumer systems, (d) evaluation of data quality rule execution records in the RDS rules engine (Rule IDs DV-119, DV-204, DV-311, DV-404), and (e) inspection of incident and defect tickets relating to data quality (ServiceNow INC and JIRA QSYS series) for root cause and remediation follow-through. Evidence was time-bounded to FY2026 and anchored to control attestations TRC-CTRL-DA-12.3 and TRC-CTRL-DG-04.2, with witness testing by Technology Risk & Controls (TRC) completed on 2026-06-12 15:20 UTC.

Results and Observations
- Completeness: Across sampled pipelines, average daily completeness for mandatory fields was 98.7% (min 97.9%, max 99.4%) against a documented threshold of ≥98.5%. Minor shortfalls were observed in RDS-MDS-PRD-311 on 2026-02-14 due to late-arriving vendor files; ServiceNow ticket INC0109234 (opened 2026-02-14 13:45 UTC; resolved 2026-02-14 15:02 UTC) indicates on-time backfill with no downstream breach of RAE calculation windows.

Automated deduplication rule DV-404 was adjusted (change logged in CHG0056991; executed 2026-03-03 21:10 UTC) with post-change monitoring indicating sustained compliance thereafter.

Exceptions were confined to newly listed instruments within 24 hours of listing; backfills were completed same day with documented approvals.

For three elements (risk factor tenor standardization, business calendar join, and FX spot normalization), lineage narratives lacked an updated “business transformation description” following the Q1 schema revision of RAE staging. Section 9. Data Quality and Reconciliation Controls (Field Testing Results and Follow-Up)

Scope and approach
Internal Audit reviewed the design and operating effectiveness of data quality and reconciliation controls across the Quantitative Systems data supply chain supporting market risk, liquidity risk, and front-office analytics for the period 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30. Operating effectiveness testing
Testing confirmed that routine field-level validations (type, null, cardinality, referential integrity) executed as configured and produced exception files with appropriate tagging for downstream triage. For example, on 2026-05-03T05:42:11Z, ETL job QS-ETL-17 initiated ingestion for MD_EOD_EQ and completed at 2026-05-03T05:58:42Z, processing 2,345,221 equity quotes; QS-DQ-Rules flagged 1,411 records (0.06%) with null securityId, all auto-quarantined and excluded from publication per SOP-DQ-014. Audit verified timely closure and attachment of vendor case transcript (Ref: VND-CASE-584113).

Change and release management controls for Quantitative Systems are designed and operating effectively.
